occurrences.rawText: THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY
THE SOCIALIST REPUBLIC OF VIETNAM
Independence - Freedom – Happiness
LABOR CODE
Pursuant to the Constitution of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam;
The National Assembly promulgates the Labor Code.
Chapter I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1. Scope of regulation

The Labor Code provides labor standards; rights, obligations and responsibilities of employees, employers, grassroots-level employees’ representative organizations and employers’ representative organizations in industrial relations and other relations directly related to industrial relations; and state management of labor.
Article 2. Subjects of application
1. Employees, apprentices, trainees, and other workers without industrial relations.
2. Employers.
3. Foreign employees who work in Vietnam.
4. Other agencies, organizations and individuals directly related to industrial relations.
Article 3. Interpretation of terms
In this Code, the terms below are construed as follows:
1. Employee means a person who works under a labor contract, is paid with wage and is managed, controlled and supervised by an employer.
The minimum working age for an employee is 15, unless otherwise specified in Section 1 of Chapter XI herein.

2. Employer means an enterprise, an agency, an organization, a cooperative, a household or an individual that hires or employs employees under labor contracts; if the employer is an individual, he/she must have full civil act capacity.

3. Grassroots-level employees’ representative organization means an organization voluntarily established by employees working for an employer which protects employees’ rights and legitimate interests in industrial relations by collective bargaining or other forms prescribed by related law provisions on labor. Grassroots-level employees’ representative organization grassroots-level Trade Unions and employees' organizations at enterprises.
4. Employers’ representative organization means a lawfully established organization which represents and protects the employers’ rights and legitimate interests in industrial relations.

5. Industrial relation means a social relation arising from the hiring or employment and wage payment between an employee, an employer, their representative organizations and competent State agencies. Industrial relations are individual industrial relations and collective industrial relations.
6. Worker without industrial relation means a person who does not work on the basis of a labor contract.
7. Forced labor means the use of force or threat to use force or other tricks to force a person to work against his/her will.

8. Labor discrimination means the discrimination, exclusion or prioritization on the basis of race, skin color, national origin or social strata, nationality, gender, age, pregnancy status, marital status, religion, belief, political belief, disabilities family responsibilities, or HIV infection, or for the reason of establishing, joining trade unions and participating in trade union activities, which impacts on equality of employment or career opportunities.
Discrimination, exclusion or prioritization based on specialized job requirements and acts of maintaining and protecting jobs for vulnerable employees shall not be considered discrimination.

9. Sexual harassment at the workplace means any sexual behavior of any person towards another person at the workplace without being desired or accepted by that person. Workplace is any place where the employee actually works as agreed upon or assigned by the employer.
Article 4. State policies on labor

1. To guarantee the rights and legitimate interests of employees and workers without industrial relations; to encourage agreements providing employees with conditions more favorable than those provided by the labor law.
2. To guarantee the rights and legitimate interests of employers, to ensure lawful, democratic, fair and civilized labor management, and to promote their social responsibility.

3. To create favorable conditions for job creation, self-employment and vocational training and learning in order to acquire employment, and for labor-intensive production and business activities; to apply a number of provisions herein to workers without industrial relations.

4. To adopt policies on the development and distribution of human resources; to improve labor productivity; to provide vocational training, training, retraining and improvement of occupational knowledge and skills for employees; to support job maintenance and change for employees; and to give preferences for employees with high professional and technical qualifications meeting the requirements of industrial revolution, national industrialization and modernization.
5. To adopt policies on labor market development and diversify types of linkage between labor supply and demand.
6. To encourage employees and employers to hold dialogues and collective bargains to establish harmonious, stable and progressive industrial relations.
7. To ensure gender equality; to stipulate the labor regime and social policies to protect female employees as well as disabled, elderly and minor employees.
Article 5. Rights and obligations of employees
1. An employee has the following rights:

a) To work, freely choose a job, workplace or occupation, to participate in vocational training and to improve occupational skills; and suffer no discrimination, forced labor and sexual harassment at the workplace;

b) To receive a wage commensurate with his/her occupational knowledge and skills on the basis of an agreement reached with the employer; to receive labor protection and work in assured conditions of labor safety and labor hygiene; to take leaves according to the prescribed regime and annual paid-leaves, and enjoy collective welfare benefits;

c) To form, join and participate in activities of trade unions, occupational associations and other organizations in accordance with law; to request and participate in dialogues with the employer, implement democracy regulations, make collective bargains with the employer and be consulted at the workplace to protect his/her rights and legitimate interests; and to participate in management activities according to the employer’s regulations;
d) To refuse the employment which causes clear threats to his/her life and health during work performance;
dd) To unilaterally terminate the labor contract in accordance with law;
e) To go on strike.
g) Other rights according to law.
2. An employee has the following obligations:
a) To perform the labor contract, collective labor agreement and other cooperative agreements;
b) To obey labor discipline and internal working regulations; to follow lawful administration of the employer;
c) To implement the laws on labor, occupation, vocational training, social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, labor safety and labor hygiene.
Article 6. Rights and obligations of employers
1. An employer has the following rights:
a) To recruit, arrange, manage, control and supervise employees; to perform commendation work and handle violations of labor discipline;
b) To form, join and operate in employers’ representative organizations, occupational associations and other organizations in accordance with law;

c) To request the employees’ representative organizations to have dialogue with the purpose of negotiating and signing a collective labor agreement; to participate in the resolution of labor disputes and strikes; to have dialogue and exchange opinions with employees’ representative organizations on issues related to industrial relations and improvement of the material and spiritual lives of employees;
d) To temporarily close the workplace.
dd) Other rights in accordance with law.
2. An employer has the following obligations:
a) To perform the labor contracts, collective labor agreement and other lawful agreements; to respect the honor and dignity of employees;
b) To establish a mechanism for and hold dialogue with the employees and their representative organizations; to implement the regulations on grassroots-level democracy at the workplace;
c) To provide training, retraining and improvement of occupational knowledge and skills for employees serving the job maintenance and change for employees;

d) To implement other provisions of law on labor, occupation, vocational training, social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, labor safety and labor hygiene; to elaborate and implement solutions for preventing and controlling sexual harassment at the workplace;
dd) To participate in developing national occupational skill standards, to assess and recognize occupational skills for employees.
Article 7. Establishment of industrial relations

1. Industrial relations shall be established through dialogue, negotiation and agreement based on the principles of voluntariness, good faith, equality, cooperation and mutual respect for each other’s rights and legitimate interests.

2. The employers, the employers’ representative organizations and the employees, the employees’ representative organizations shall establish progressive, harmonious and stable industrial relations with supports of competent State agencies.

3. Trade unions shall, in collaboration with competent State agencies, facilitate the establishment of progressive, harmonious and stable industrial relations; supervise the implementation of the labor law; and protect the rights and legitimate interests of employees and employers.

4. The Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the Vietnam Cooperatives’ Union and other lawfully established employers' representative organizations shall act as representatives to protect employers’ rights and legitimate interests and participate in establishing progressive, harmonious and stable industrial relations.
Article 8. Prohibited acts in the field of labor
1. Labor discrimination.
2. Maltreating employees and forcing labor.
3. Committing sexual harassment at the workplace.

4. Making use of apprenticeship or on-the-job training for the purpose of self-seeking and exploiting labor or enticing or compelling apprentices or on-the-job trainees to carry out illegal activities.

5. Using employees who have no vocational training or national occupational skills certificates for the occupations or jobs which require employees who have received vocational training or national occupational skills certificates.

6. Enticing, promising or making false advertising or other tricks to deceive employees or to employ employees for trafficking in persons and forced labor, or making use of employment services or the sending of labor to work abroad under contracts to commit illegal acts.
7. Illegally using minor employees.
Chapter II EMPLOYMENT, RECRUITMENT AND LABOR MANAGEMENT
Article 9. Employment and creation of employment
1. Employment is any income-generating laboring activity that is not prohibited by law.
2. The State, employers and the society have the responsibility to create employment and guarantee that all people with working ability have access to employment opportunities.
Article 10. The right of employees to work
1. To freely choose a job, work for any employer in any location that is not prohibited by law.
2. To directly contact an employer or through an employment service institution in order to find a job that meets his/her expectation, capacity, occupational qualification, and health.
Article 11. Recruitment of employees
1. An employer has the right to recruit labor directly or through employment service institutions and labor leasing enterprises to recruit employees in accordance with the labor demand.
2. Employees shall not pay fees for their recruitment.
Article 12. Employers’ responsibilities for labor management
1. To make, update, manage and use labor management books in paper or electronic form and present them at the request of competent State agencies.

2. To report on the employment of employees within 30 days from the date of operation commencement, to periodically report about labor changes in the course of operation to the specialized labor agencies of the provincial-level People's Committees and notify the social insurance agencies.
3. The Government shall detail this Article.
Chapter III
LABOR CONTRACT
Section 1
ENTRY INTO LABOR CONTRACTS
Article 13. Labor contract
1. Labor contract is an agreement between an employee and an employer on a paid job, wages, working conditions, and the rights and obligations of each party in industrial relations.

If the two parties’ agreement is called by another name with the contents related to a paid job, wages and the management, administration and supervision of one party, it shall be considered as a labor contract.
2. Before accepting an employee, the employer and the employee shall enter into a labor contract.
Article 14. Forms of labor contract
1. A labor contract must be established in writing and made in 02 copies, one to be kept by the employee and the other by the employer, unless otherwise stated in Clause 2 of this Article.
A labor contract established via electronic means in the form of data messages in accordance with the law on electronic transactions is valid as a written labor contract.

2. The parties may enter into a verbal labor contract for jobs with a duration of under 01 month, unless otherwise stated in Clause 2 of Article 18, Point a, Clause 1 of Article 145 and Clause 1 of Article 162 herein.
Article 15. Principles of entry into a labor contract
1. Voluntariness, fairness, good faith, cooperation and honesty.
2. Freedom to enter into a labor contract which is not contrary to the law, the collective labor agreement and social morality.
Article 16. Obligation to provide information before entering into a labor contract

1. An employer shall provide an employee with reliable information about the job, workplace, working conditions, working hours, rest time, occupational safety and hygiene, wage, forms of wage payment, social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, regulations on business confidentiality, technological confidentiality, and other issues directly related to the entry into the labor contract as requested by the employee.

2. The employee shall provide the employer with reliable information about his/her full name, age, gender, residence address, education level, occupational skills and qualification, certificate of health conditions and other issues directly related to the entry into a labor contract as requested by the employer.
Article 17. Prohibited acts of employers when entering into and performing labor contracts
1. Keeping the employees’ original identity cards, diplomas and certificates.
2. Requesting employees to make a deposit in cash or property as security for the performance of labor contracts.
3. Forcing employees to perform labor contracts in order to pay debts to employers.
Article 18. Competence to enter into labor contracts
1. Employees shall directly enter into labor contracts, unless otherwise specified in Clause 2 of this Article.

2. For seasonal jobs or certain jobs with a definite term of less than 12 months, a group of employees who are full 18 years old or more shall authorize an employee in the group to enter into a labor contract; in this case, the labor contract must be established in writing and have the same effect as with each employee.
The labor contract signed by the authorized employee must be enclosed with a list clearly stating the full name, date of birth, gender, residence address and signature of each employee.
3. The person entering into a labor contract on the employer's side is one of the following persons:
a) The representative at law of the enterprise or the authorized person as prescribed by law;
b) The head of an agency or organization with legal status according as prescribed by law or the authorized person as prescribed by law;
c) The representative of a household, a cooperative group or other organizations without legal status or authorized persons as prescribed by law;
d) The individual directly using the employees.
4. The person entering into a labor contract on the employee's side is one of the following persons:
a) The employee who is full 18 years old or more;
b) The employee who is from 15 to under 18 years old with written consent of his/her representative at law;
c) The person who is under 15 and his/her legal representative;
d) The employee legally authorized to enter into a labor contract by employees in a group.
5. Persons who are authorized to enter into labor contracts shall not authorize others to enter into the labor contracts.
Article 19. Entry into more than one labor contract
1. An employee may enter into labor contracts with more than one employer, provided that he/she fully performs all the contents of the entered contracts.

2. In case an employee enters into labor contracts with more than one employer, his/her participation in social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance shall comply with the laws on social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, and labor safety and hygiene.
Article 20. Types of labor contract
1. A labor contract must be entered into in one of the following types:
a) An indefinite-term labor contract is a contract in which the two parties do not determine the duration and the time of termination of the contract;

b) A definite-term labor contract is a contract in which the two parties determine the duration and the time of termination of the contract within less than 36 months from the effective date of the contract.
2. When a labor contract prescribed at Point b, Clause 1 of this Article expires and the employee continues working, it shall comply as follows:

a) Within 30 days from the date of expiration of the contract, the two parties shall sign a new labor contract; pending the signing of a new labor contract, the rights, obligations and interests of both parties shall be performed in accordance with the contract already entered into;

b) If no new labor contract is entered into within 30 days from the date of expiration of the contract, the contract entered into under Point b, Clause 1 of this Article shall become an indefinite-term labor contract;

c) In case the two parties enter into a new labor contract with a definite term, only 01 additional definite-term labor contract may be signed; after that, if the employee continues working, an indefinite-term contract must be entered into, except for the labor contracts entered into by persons hired as directors of State-invested enterprises and other cases specified at Clause 1 of Article 149, Clause 2 of Article 151 and Clause 4 of Article 177 herein.
Article 21. Contents of a labor contract
1. A labor contract must have the following principal contents:
a) Name and address of the employer or full name, position of the person entering into a labor contract on the employer's side;
b) Full name, date of birth, gender, residence address, number of identity card or passport of the person entering into a labor contract on the employee's side;
c) Job and workplace;
d) Term of the labor contract;
dd) Wage in accordance with the job or position, form of wage payment, deadline for wage payment, wage-based allowances and other additional payments;
e) Regimes for promotion and wage raise;
g) Working time, rest time;
h) Labor protection equipment for the employee;
i) Social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance;
k) Training, retraining and occupational skill improvement.

2. When an employee performs a job which is directly related to business or technology secrets as prescribed by law, the employer shall reach a written agreement with the employee on the content and duration of protection of business or technology secrets, and benefits and compensation in case of violation.

3. For employees working in agriculture, forestry, fishery or salt production, based on the type of job, both parties may skip some principal contents of the labor contract and reach additional agreements on settlement measures when the contract performance is affected by natural disaster, fire or weather.
4. The Government shall stipulate the contents of a labor contract with an employee who is hired to work as director of a State-invested enterprise.
5. The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall detail Clauses 1, 2 and 3 of this Article.
Article 22. Annexes to a labor contract
1. An annex to a labor contract is a part of the labor contract and is as valid as the labor contract.
2. An annex to a labor contract details, amends or supplements some provisions of the contract without changing the duration of the contract.
In case an annex to a labor contract details some provisions that lead to a different understanding of the labor contract, the contents of the labor contract prevail.
In case an annex amends or supplements some provisions of the labor contract, it must specify the amended or supplemented provisions and the time they take effect.
Article 23. Effectiveness of a labor contract
A labor contract takes effect on the date it is entered into by the parties, unless otherwise agreed upon by both parties or provided by law.
Article 24. Probation
1. An employer and an employee may reach agreement on probation stated on a labor contract or enter into a probation contract.
2. A probation contract must have the probation period and contents specified at Points a, b, c, dd, g and h, Clause 1 of Article 21 herein.
3. Employees working under labor contracts with the duration of under 01 month are not subject to probation.
Article 25. Probationary period
The probation period must be agreed upon by the two parties based on the nature and complexity of the job, but probation is applied only once for each job and assure the following conditions:

1. It does not exceed 180 days for the enterprise manager as prescribed by the Law on Enterprises, the Law on Management and use of state capital invested in business and production at the enterprise;
2. It does not exceed 60 days for posts which require professional and technical qualifications of collegial or higher level;
3. It does not exceed 30 days for posts which require professional and technical qualifications of intermediate level, or for technical workers and skilled employees;
4. It does not exceed 06 working days for other types of jobs.
Article 26. Wage during the probationary period
The wage for an employee during the probation period shall be agreed upon by the two parties but must be at least equal to 85% of the wage for the job.
Article 27. Expiry of the probation period
1. At the end of the probationary period, the employer must notify the probation result to the employee.

If the probational job is satisfactory, the employer shall continue to perform the labor contract entered into with agreement upon probation or shall sign a labor contract with the employee who entered into a probation contract.
If the probational job is unsatisfactory, the entered labor contract or the probation contract shall be terminated.
2. During the probation period, each party may cancel the entered labor contract or the probation contract without prior notice and compensation.
Section 2 PERFORMANCE OF LABOR CONTRACTS
Article 28. Performance of jobs under a labor contract

The jobs under a labor contract must be performed by the employee who has entered into the contract. The workplace may be as indicated in the labor contract or otherwise agreed upon between the two parties.
Article 29. Assignment of employees to perform jobs which are not stated in labor contracts

1. When meeting with sudden difficulties such as natural disaster, fire or epidemic, or taking measures to prevent and deal with a working accident, an occupational disease, an electricity or water supply incident, or when due to business and production needs, the employer may temporarily assign an employee to perform a job which is not stated in the labor contract provided that the assignment does not exceed 60 accumulated workdays within 01 year; the assignment exceeding 60 accumulated workdays within 01 year must be agreed by the employee.

The employer shall specify in the labor regulations the cases where, due to production and business needs, the employer may temporarily assign the employee to perform a job which is not stated in the labor contract.

2. When an employer temporarily assigns an employee to perform the job which is not stated the labor contract as prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article, the employer shall inform the employee at least 03 working days in advance, clearly stating the duration of temporary job, and assign the job which must be suitable to the health and gender of the employee.

3. The employee who performs a job which is not stated the labor contract is entitled to a wage for the new job. If the wage for the new job is lower than the previous wage, he/she is entitled to the previous wage for 30 working days. The wage for the new job must be at least 85% of the previous wage but not lower than the minimum wage.

4. If an employee does not agree to temporarily perform a job which is not stated the labor contract for more than 60 accumulated workdays within 01 year and has to stop working, the employer must pay the wage in case of work suspension as prescribed in Article 99 herein.
Article 30. Suspension of a labor contract
1. Cases of suspension of a labor contract:
a) The employee is called up for military service or participates in the Militia and Self-Defense Force;
b) The employee is held in custody or detention in accordance with the criminal procedure law;
c) The employee is subject to a decision on application of the measure of consignment to a reformatory, compulsory drug detoxification center or compulsory education institution;
d) The female employee is pregnant in accordance with Article 138 herein;
dd) The employee is appointed to be the manager of the enterprise of a one-member limited liability company in which the State holds 100% of the charter capital;
e) The employee is authorized to exercise the rights and responsibilities of the ownership representative for the State capital portion at the enterprise;
g) The employee is authorized to exercise the rights and responsibilities of the enterprise for the enterprise’s capital invested in another enterprise;
h) Other cases as agreed by both parties.

2. During the suspension of a labor contract, the employee is not entitled to the salary and the rights and interests already stated in the entered labor contract, unless otherwise agreed by the two parties or prescribed by law.
Article 31. Reinstatement of employees upon expiry of the period of suspension of labor contracts

Within 15 days after the expiry of the period of suspension of a labor contract, the employee shall show up at the workplace and the employer shall reinstate the employee as prescribed in the entered labor contract if the contract does not expires, unless otherwise agreed upon by the two parties or prescribed by law.
Article 32. Part-time employees

1. Part-time employee is a person who works for less than the normal daily or weekly or monthly working hours as provided by the labor law, the collective labor agreement or the employer’s regulations.
2. An employee shall negotiate with the employer on working on a part-time basis when entering into a labor contract.

3. Part-time employees are entitled to a wage and have the same rights and obligations as full-time employees and are entitled to equal opportunities and to non-discrimination and assured labor safety and hygiene.
Article 33. Modification and supplementation of a labor contract

1. During the performance of a labor contract, any party that requests to modify or supplement the contents of the labor contract shall notify at least 03 working days in advance to the other party of the contents to be modified or supplemented.

2. In case the two parties can reach an agreement, the modification or supplementation of the labor contract must be carried out by signing an annex to the labor contract or signing a new labor contract.
3. In case the two parties cannot reach an agreement on the modification or supplementation of the labor contract, they shall continue performing the labor contract already entered into.
Section 3
TERMINATION OF LABOR CONTRACTS
Article 34. Cases of termination of a labor contract
1. The labor contract expires, unless otherwise specified in Clause 4, Article 177 herein.
2. The work stated in the labor contract has been completed.
3. Both parties agree to terminate the labor contract.

4. The employee is sentenced to imprisonment but is not entitled to a suspended sentence or does not fall into the case of being released as prescribed in Clause 5, Article 328 of the Criminal Procedure Code, or is sentenced to death or is prohibited from performing the job stated in the labor contract under a legally effective judgment or ruling of a court.
5. The foreign employee working in Vietnam is expelled under the legally effective judgments or decisions of competent State agencies.
6. The employee dies or is declared by a court to have lost civil act capacity, be missing or dead.

7. The individual employer dies or is declared by a court to have lost civil act capacity, be missing or dead. The institutional employer terminates operation or declared by the business registration agency of the provincial-level People's Committee to have no representative at law or authorized person performing the rights and obligations of the representative at law.
8. The employee is dismissed.
9. The employee unilaterally terminates the labor contract under Article 35 herein.
10. The employer unilaterally terminates the labor contract under Article 36 herein.
11. The employer lays off the employee in accordance with Articles 42 and 43 herein.
12. The labor permit of a foreigner employee working in Vietnam under Article 156 herein.
13. The probation job is unsatisfactory to the probation agreement stated in the labor contract or one party cancels the probation agreement.
Article 35. The right of employees to unilaterally terminate labor contracts
1. An employee may unilaterally terminate the labor contract and must notify the employer in advance:
a) At least 45 days if working under an indefinite-term labor contract;
b) At least 30 days if working under a definite-term labor contract with a term of 12 months to 36 months;
c) At least 03 working days if working under a definite-term labor contracts with a term of less than 12 months;
d) For work-specific labor, the notification period shall comply with the Government's regulations.
2. An employee may unilaterally terminate the labor contract without prior notice as follows:
a) He/she is not assigned to the job or workplace or is not given the working conditions as agreed in the labor contract, unless otherwise specified in Article 29 herein;
b) He/she is not paid in full or on time as agreed in the labor contract, unless otherwise specified in Clause 4, Article 97 herein;
c) He/she is maltreated, beaten, verbally and physically humiliated with effects on his/her health, dignity and honor, or is subject to forced labor;
d) He/she is sexually harassed at the workplace;
dd) A female employee who is pregnant and must take leave as prescribed in Clause 1 of Article 138 herein;
e) He/she reaches retirement age as prescribed in Article 169 herein, unless otherwise agreed by the parties;
g) An employer provides unreliable information as prescribed in Clause 1, Article 16 herein, which affects the performance of the labor contract.
Article 36. The right of employers to unilaterally terminate labor contracts
1. An employer may unilaterally terminate a labor contract in the following cases:

a) The employee often fails to perform his/her job stated in the labor contract determined by the criteria to assess the job performance in the employer's regulations. The regulations on assessment of job performance shall be issued by the employer and must be revised by the grassroots-level employees’ representative organization if such organization exist;

b) The employee is sick or has an accident and remains unable to work after having received treatment for 12 consecutive months, in case he/she works under an indefinite-term labor contract, or for 06 consecutive months, in case he/she works under a definite-term labor contract with a term of from 12 to 36 months, or more than half the term of the labor contract, in case he/she works under a labor contract for a definite-term job or a specific job of under 12 months.
When the employee’s health has recovered, he/she must be considered for continued entry into the labor contract with the employer;

c) If, as a result of natural disaster, fire, epidemic or enemy sabotage, or relocating and scaling down production and business at the request of competent State agencies, the employer, though having applied every remedial measure, has to cut jobs;
d) The employee is absent from the workplace after the time limit specified in Article 31 herein.
dd) The employee reaches retirement age as prescribed in Article 169 herein, unless otherwise agreed by the parties;
e) The employee quits his/her job without plausible reasons for more than 05 consecutive working days;
g) The employee provides unreliable information under Clause 2, Article 16 herein when entering into labor contracts, thus affecting his/her recruitment.
2. When unilaterally terminating a labor contract as prescribed at Points a, b, c, dd and g or Clause 1 of this Article, the employer shall notify the employee in advance:
a) At least 45 days, for indefinite-term labor contracts;
b) At least 30 days, for definite-term labor contracts with a term of from 12 to 36 months;
c) At least 03 working days if working under a definite-term labor contracts with a term of less than 12 months and cases stipulated at Point b, Clause 1 of this Article;
d) For work-specific labor, the notification period shall comply with the Government's regulations.
3. When unilaterally terminating a labor contract prescribed at Points d and e, Clause 1 of this Article, the employer shall not notify the employee in advance.
Article 37. Cases in which an employer is prohibited from unilaterally terminating a labor contract

1. The employee is sick or has a work accident or occupational disease and is being treated or nursed under the decision of a competent health establishment, unless otherwise specified at Point b, Clause 1 of Article 36 herein.
2. The employee is on annual leave, personal leave or any other types of leave permitted by the employer.
3. The female employee is pregnant; the employee is on maternity leave or the employee is taking care of his/her small child who is under 12 months old.
Article 38. Cancellation of unilateral termination of a labor contract

Each party may cancel its unilateral termination of the labor contract at any time prior to the expiry of the time limit for prior notice provided that a written notification is sent to and such cancellation is agreed by the other party.
Article 39. Illegal unilateral termination of a labor contract
The unilateral termination of a labor contract is illegal in the cases which do not comply with Articles 35, 36 and 37 herein.
Article 40. Obligations of an employee when unilaterally terminating a labor contract illegally
1. Not to be entitled to a severance allowance.

2. To compensate the employer half of a month’s wage in accordance with the labor contract and an amount equivalent to the wage in accordance with the labor contract for working days without prior notice.
3. To reimburse training costs to the employer in accordance with Article 62 of this Code.
Article 41. Obligations of an employer when unilaterally terminating a labor contract illegally

1. To reinstate the employee in accordance with the entered labor contract; to pay the wage, social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance premiums for the days during which the employee was not allowed to work, and an additional amount equal to at least 02 months’ wage in accordance with the labor contract.
After being reinstated, the employee shall reimburse the received severance allowances and job-loss allowances if any to the employer.
In case the position or job agreed in the labor contract is no longer vacant and the employee still wishes to work, both parties shall negotiate to modify and supplement the labor contract.

If violating the provision on the time of prior notice as prescribed in Clause 2 of Article 36 herein, the employer shall compensate the employee an amount equivalent to his/her wage in accordance with the labor contract for the working days without prior notice.

2. In case the employee does not wish to return to work, in addition to the compensation prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article, the employer shall pay a severance allowance in accordance with Article 46 herein in order to terminate the labor contract.

3. In case the employer does not want to reinstate the employee and the employee agrees, in addition to the compensation prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article and the severance allowance prescribed in Article 46 herein, the two parties shall negotiate on an additional compensation which must be at least equal to 02 months’ wage in accordance with the labor contract in order to terminate the labor contract.
Article 42. Obligations of an employer in case of changing structure, technology or economic reasons
1. The following cases are considered structural and technological change:
a) Changing the organizational structure, reorganizing labor;
b) Changing the process, technology, machinery and equipment for production and business associated with the production and business lines of the employer;
c) Changing the product or product structure.
2. The following cases are considered as economic reasons:
a) Economic crisis or recession;
b) Implementing policies and laws of the State when restructuring the economy or implementing international commitments.

3. In case there is a change in the structure or technology that affects the employment of many employees, the employer shall elaborate and implement a labor utilization plan in accordance with Article 44 herein; in case new jobs are created, priority must be given to re-training these employees for continued employment.

4. In case more than one employee face the risk of unemployment or forced dismissal because of economic reasons, the employer shall elaborate and implement a labor utilization plan in accordance with Article 44 here in.
5. In case the employer cannot employ and have to dismiss employees, the employer shall pay job-loss allowances to the employees in accordance with Article 47 herein.

6. The dismissal of employees in accordance with this Article shall be implemented only after discussion with the grassroots-level employees’ representative organization of which the employees are members, and notification 30 days in advance to the provincial-level People’s Committee and the employees.

Article 43. Obligations of an employer in case of split, separation, consolidation, merger; sale, lease, conversion of business type; transferring asset ownership or use rights of enterprises or cooperatives

1. In case of splitting, separating, consolidating, merging; selling, leasing, converting business type; transferring asset ownership or use rights of an enterprise an enterprise or a cooperative that effect the employment of many employees, the employer shall elaborate a labor utilization plan in accordance with Article 44 herein.
2. The current employer and the succeeding employer are responsible for implementing the approved labor utilization plan.
3. Employees who are dismissed shall receive job-loss allowances in accordance with Article 47 herein.
Article 44. Labor utilization plan
1. A labor utilization plan must have the following principal contents:
a) The lists and numbers of employees to be further employed, employees to be re-trained for continued employment and employees to be assigned part-time jobs;
b) The list and number of employees to be retired;
c) The lists and numbers of employees to terminate their labor contracts;
d) Rights and obligations of the employer, the employee and relevant parties in the implementation of the labor utilization plan;
dd) Measures and financial sources for implementing the plan.

2. When elaborating a labor utilization plan, the employer must discuss with the grassroots-level employees’ representative organization for the place where such organization exists. The labor utilization plan must be publicly notified to the employees within 15 days from the date of adoption.
Article 45. Notice of termination of a labor contract

1. The employer must notify the employee in writing of the termination of the labor contract when it terminates as prescribed herein, unless otherwise specified in Clauses 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, Article 34 herein.
2. In case the institutional employer terminates its operation, the time of termination of the labor contract is the time of notification of operation termination.

In case the institutional employer declared by the business registration agency of the provincial-level People's Committee to have no representative at law or authorized person performing the rights and obligations of the representative at law as prescribed in Clause 7 of Article 34 herein, the time of termination of the labor contract is the date of declaration.
Article 46. Severance allowance

1. In case a labor contract terminates in accordance with Clauses 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9 and 10 of Article 34 herein, the employer shall pay a severance allowance to the employee who has worked regularly for full 12 months or longer at the rate of half of a month’s wage for each working year, except for those eligible of pension in accordance with the law on social insurance and those specified at Point e of Clause 1, Article 36 herein.

2. The working period used for the calculation of severance allowance is the total period during which the employee actually works for the employer minus the period during which the employee benefits from unemployment insurance in accordance with the law on social insurance, and the working period for which the employer has paid a severance allowance or job-loss allowance to the employee.
3. The wage used for the calculation of severance allowance is the average wage in accordance with the labor contract for 6 consecutive months preceding the time the employee loses his/her job.
4. The Government shall detail this Article.
Article 47. Job-loss allowance

1. An employer shall pay a job-loss allowance to an employee who has worked regularly for the employer for 12 months or longer and loses his/her job under Clause 11 of Article 34 herein. The job-loss allowance is equal to 1 month’s wage for each working year but must not be lower than 2 months’ wage.

2. The working period used for the calculation of job-loss allowance is the total time during which the employee actually works for the employer minus the time during which the employee benefits from unemployment insurance in accordance with the law on unemployment insurance and the working period for which the employer has paid a severance allowance or job-loss allowance to the employee.
3. The wage used for the calculation of job-loss allowance is the average wage in accordance with the labor contract for 6 consecutive months preceding the time the employee loses his/her job.
4. The Government shall detail this Article.
Article 48. Responsibilities in case of terminating labor contracts

1. Within 14 working days after termination of a labor contract, the two parties shall make all payments related to the interests of each party; this time limit may be extended but must not exceed 30 days in the following cases:
a) The institutional employer terminates its operation;
b) The employer changes the structure, technology or for economic reasons;
c) In case of splitting, separating, consolidating, merging; selling, leasing, converting business type; transferring asset ownership or use rights of an enterprise an enterprise or a cooperative;
d) In case of natural disaster, fire, enemy sabotage or epidemic.

2. The payment of wages, social insurance, health insurance, unemployment insurance, severance allowances and other benefits of its employees according to the collective labor agreement and signed labor contracts shall be prioritized in case an enterprise or a cooperative has its operation terminated, is dissolved or goes bankrupt.
3. The employer shall:
a) Complete the confirmation procedure for payment time of social insurance and unemployment insurance and return it with other papers of the employee which are kept by the employer;
b) Provide copies of documents related to the working process of the employee if the employee so requests. The cost of copying and sending documents shall be paid by the employer.
Section 4 INVALID LABOR CONTRACTS
Article 49. Invalid labor contracts
1. A labor contract is wholly invalid in one of the following cases:
a) The whole contents of the labor contract are illegal;
b) The individual enters into the labor contract ultra vires or violate the principles of entry into labor contracts specified in Clause 1 of Article 15 herein;
c) The job agreed upon in the labor contract is prohibited by law.
2. A labor contract is partially invalid when one of its contents is illegal but does not affect the remaining contents of the labor contract.
Article 50. Competence to declare labor contract to be invalid
The people’s courts are competent to declare labor contracts to be invalid.
Article 51. Handling of invalid labor contracts
1. A labor contract which is declared to be partially invalid will be handled as follows:

a) The rights, obligations and benefits of the parties must be settled according to the applicable collective labor agreements; in case the collective labor agreements do not exist, the provisions of laws prevail;
b) The two parties must modify and supplement the part of the labor contract which is declared invalid to conform with the collective labor agreement or the labor law.

2. In case a labor contract is declared to be wholly invalid, the rights, obligations and benefits of the employee will be settled in accordance with law; in case it is signed ultra vires, the parties shall re-sign it.
3. The Government shall detail this Article.
Section 5 LABOR LEASE
Article 52. Labor lease

1. Labor lease means that an employee enters into a labor contract with an employer who is a labor leasing enterprise, after which the employee is transferred to work and managed by the other employer while still maintaining industrial relations with the leasing enterprise.
2. Labor lease is a conditional business line performed by only enterprises licensed for labor lease and applicable only to certain jobs.
Article 53. Principles of labor lease
1. The maximum duration of labor lease for employees is 12 months.
2. The hiring party may use the leased employees in the following cases:
a) Temporarily meeting a sudden increase in the labor demand in a given period;
b) Replacing employees during maternity leave, employees who have labor accidents, occupational disease or employees who are fulfilling citizen obligations;
c) There is a need to use employees with rich professional knowledge and high technical qualifications.
3. The hiring party may not use the leased employees in the following cases:
a) Replacing employees who are in the process of exercising the right to go on strikes or settling labor disputes;
b) There is no specific agreement on the labor leasing enterprise’s responsibility for compensation to the leased employees in case of labor accidents and occupational diseases;
c) Replacing employees who are fired due to changes in structure, technology, or economic reasons, or split, separation, consolidation or merger.
4. The hiring party shall not assign the leased employees to another employer; not use the leased employees assigned by the unlicensed labor leasing enterprises.
Article 54. Labor leasing enterprises
1. A labor leasing enterprise shall pay a deposit and obtain a license for labor lease.
2. The Government shall provide the payment of deposits, the conditions and procedures for granting, regranting and extending licenses of labor lease, and the list of jobs allowed for labor lease.
Article 55. Labor leasing contract
1. The labor leasing enterprise and the hiring party shall sign a written labor leasing contract, which is made in 2 copies, each to be kept by one party.
2. A labor leasing contract must contain the following principal contents:
a) Location of the workplace, working position for the leased employee, detailed description of the job and specific requirements for the leased employee;
b) Duration of the lease; the starting time of the lease;
c) Working time, rest time, occupational safety and hygiene conditions at the workplace;
d) Responsibility for compensation for labor accidents and occupational diseases;
dd) Obligations of each party toward the leased employee.

3. The labor leasing contract must not contain any agreement on the rights and benefits of the employee that are less favorable than those agreed upon in the labor contract signed between the employee and the labor leasing enterprise.
Article 56. Rights and obligations of a labor leasing enterprise
In addition to the rights and obligations prescribed in Article 6 herein, a labor leasing enterprise has the following rights and obligations:
1. To ensure supply of a skilled employee who meets the requirements of the hiring party and the labor contract signed with the employee;
2. To inform the leased employee of the contents of the labor leasing contract;
3. To provide the hiring party with a brief personal record of the leased employee and his/her demands;
4. To ensure that the wage of the leased employee is not lower than that of a normal employee of the hiring party who has the same qualification and performs the same job or job of equal value;
5. To make a dossier stating the number of leased employees and the hiring party, and periodically report them to the specialized agency in charge of labor of the provincial-level People’s Committee;
6. To discipline leased employees violating labor discipline who are returned by the hiring party for their violations of labor discipline.
Article 57. Rights and obligations of the hiring party
1. To inform and guide the leased employee to understand its internal working regulations and other regulations.
2. Not to discriminate between the leased employee and its own employees regarding working conditions.
3. To negotiate with the leased employee on working at night or overtime as prescribed herein.

4. To negotiate with the leased employee and the labor leasing enterprise in order to officially employ this employee in case the labor contract between the leased employee and the labor leasing enterprise have not yet expired.
5. To return to the labor leasing enterprise the leased employee who fails to meet the requirements as agreed or who violates labor discipline.
6. To provide evidence of the leased employee’s violation of labor discipline for the labor leasing enterprise to consider and discipline such employee.
Article 58. Rights and obligations of a leased employee
In addition to the rights and obligations prescribed in Article 5 herein, a leased employee has the following rights and obligations:
1. To perform the job under the labor contract signed with the labor leasing enterprise;
2. To comply with the labor discipline, internal labor regulations; the lawful management, control and supervision of the hiring party;
3. To be paid with a wage not lower than that of employees of the hiring party who have the same qualification and perform the same job or job of equal value;
4. To lodge a complaint with the labor leasing enterprise when the hiring party violates agreements in the labor leasing contract.;
5. To negotiate to terminate the labor contract with the labor leasing enterprise to sign a labor contract with the hiring party.
Chapter IV VOCATIONAL EDUCATION AND TRAINING, AND OCCUPATIONAL SKILL IMPROVEMENT
Article 59. Vocational training and occupational skill improvement

1. An employee is entitled to freely choose vocational training, participate in assessment and recognition of national occupational skills, or develop occupational competency, which is appropriate to his/her employment demand and capability.

2. The State shall encourage any eligible employer to carry out vocational training or occupational skill improvement for its current employees and other employees in the society through the activities as follows:

a) Establishing a vocational training institution or opening vocational training classes at the workplace in order to train and retrain for improving occupational qualifications and skills for the employees; coordinating with vocational training institutions to open elementary, intermediate or collegial vocational training programs and other training programs in accordance with law;

b) Organizing occupational skill testing for employees; participating in an occupational skill council; forecasting the demand and elaborating occupational skill standards; organizing occupational skill assessment and recognition; developing occupational competency for employees.
Article 60. Responsibilities of an employer for training, retraining and improving vocational qualifications and skills

1. An employer shall prepare annual training plans and budgets for training, retraining and improving vocational qualifications and skills for his/her current employees and training for employees before switching them to perform other jobs for the employer.

2. An employer shall annually report on the results of training, retraining and improving vocational qualifications and skills to the specialized agency in charge of labor under the provincial-level People’s Committee.
Article 61. Apprenticeship and on-the-job training to work for the employer

1. Apprenticeship to work for an employer is an employer's recruitment of an employee to conduct vocational training for him/her at the workplace. Duration of apprenticeship on the training program of each level shall comply with the Law on Vocational Education and Training.

2. On-the-job training to work for an employer is an employer's recruitment of an employee to give job-practice and job-training in accordance with his/her recruited position at the workplace. Duration of on-the-job training shall not exceed 03 months.

3. An employer that recruits apprentices or on-the-job trainees to work for him/her does not have to register such vocational training activity; may not collect tuition fees; and shall enter into a vocational training contract in accordance with the Law on Vocational Education and Training.

4. An apprentice or on-the-job trainee must be full 14 years old or more and have appropriate health conditions required by the relevant apprenticeship and on-the-job training. The apprentices or on-the-job trainees of some occupations specified on the list of heavy, hazardous, dangerous occupations or extremely heavy, hazardous and dangerous occupations issued by the Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs must be full 18 years old or more, except for those working in arts, physical training and sports.

5. During the period of apprenticeship or on-the-job training, if the apprentice or the on-the-job trainee directly makes, or participates in the making of, products, he/she must be paid with a wage by the employer at a level agreed by the two parties.
6. Upon the expiry of the apprenticeship or on-the-job training period, the two parties shall enter into a labor contract as conditions prescribed herein are met.
Article 62. Vocational training contract between an employer and an employee, and job training expenses

1. The two parties shall enter into a vocational training contract in case the employee will be trained for vocational qualification and skill improvement or re-trained at home or abroad with the employer’s fund, including the fund donated by the employer’s partner.
A vocational training contract must be made in 2 copies, each to be kept by one party.
2. A vocational training contract must have the following principal contents:
a) The trained occupation;
b) Training venue, training period and wages paid in the training period;
c) The period during which the employee commits to working for the employer after training;
d) Training expenses and responsibility to reimburse training expenses;
dd) Responsibilities of the employer;
e) Responsibilities of the employee.

3. Training expenses are those accompanied by valid documents on payment for trainers, training materials, training venues, machinery and equipment, practicing materials, support for trainees, wages, social insurance, health insurance and unemployment premiums paid for trainees during the training. In case an employee is sent to a foreign country for training, training expenses also include travel and living expenses during the period of training.
Chapter V DIALOGUE AT WORKPLACE, COLLECTIVE BARGAINING, COLLECTIVE LABOR AGREEMENTS
Section 1 DIALOGUE AT WORKPLACE
Article 63. Conducting of dialogue at workplace

1. Dialogue at the workplace is the sharing of information, reference, discussion and exchange of opinions between employers and employees or their representative organizations on issues related to the rights, interests and concerns of the parties at the workplace to enhance understanding, cooperation, and make efforts towards solutions for mutual benefits.
2. An employer shall conduct dialogue at the workplace:
a) At least once a year;
b) At the request of one or both parties;
c) In the cases as prescribed in Point a of Clause 1, Article 36, Articles 42, 44, 93, 104, 118 and Clause 1 of Article 128 herein.
3. Employers and employees or their representative organizations are encouraged to conduct dialogues in the cases other than prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article.
4. The Government shall provide for the conducting of dialogue and implementation of grassroots-level democracy at the workplace.
Article 64. Issues of dialogue at workplace
1. The issues of dialogue at workplace shall comply with Point c, Clause 2, Article 63 herein.
2. In addition to the issues specified in Clause 1 of this Article, the parties may discuss one or several of the following issues in a dialogue:
a) Production and business situation of the employer;
b) Performance of labor contracts, collective labor agreement, internal regulations and other commitments and agreements at workplace;
c) Working conditions;
d) Requests of individual employees and the employees’ representative organizations to the employer;
dd) Requests of the employer to individual employees and the employees’ representative organizations;
e) Other issues which concern one or both parties.
Section 2 COLLECTIVE BARGAINING
Article 65. Collective bargaining

Collective bargaining is the discussion and negotiation between one party which is one or several employees’ representative organizations and the other party which is one or several employers or employers’ representative organizations in order to establish working conditions, regulate the relations between the parties and build harmonious, stable and progressive industrial relations.
Article 66. Principles of collective bargaining
Collective bargaining must be carried out on the principles of voluntariness, cooperativeness, good faith, equality, publicity and transparency.
Article 67. Issues for collective bargaining
The parties shall discuss one or several of the following issues in collective bargaining:
1. Wages, allowances, pay rise, bonuses, meals and other policies;
2. Workload and working time, rest time, overtime work, mid-shift breaks;
3. Ensuring employment for employees;
4. Ensuring occupational safety and hygiene; implementation of the internal working regulations;
5. Conditions and means of operation of the employees’ representative organization; relations between the employer and the employees’ representative organization;
6. Mechanisms and methods for preventing and settling labor disputes;
7. Ensuring gender equality, maternity protection, annual leaves; preventing violence and sexual harassment at the workplace;
8. Other issues that concern one or both parties.
Article 68. The right to request collective bargaining of the grassroots-level employees’ representative organization at an enterprise

1. The grassroots-level employees’ representative organizations have the right to request collective bargaining when reaching the minimum number of members in the total number of employees of an enterprise as prescribed by the Government.

2. In case an enterprise has many grassroots-level employees’ representative organizations meeting the provisions of Clause 1 of this Article, the organization has the right to request collective bargaining is the one with the largest number of members in the enterprise. Other grassroots-level employees’ representative organizations may participate in collective bargaining upon agreed by the employees’ representative organization having the right to request collective bargaining.

3. In case an enterprise has many grassroots-level employees’ representative organization, but no organization meets the provisions of Clause 1 of this Article, the organizations shall voluntarily join together to request collective bargaining, but the total number of members of these organizations must reach the minimum rate as prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article.
4. The Government shall provide for the settlement of disputes between the parties regarding the right to request collective bargaining.
Article 69. Representatives for collective bargaining at an enterprise
1. The number of persons of each party to attend a bargaining meeting must be agreed by the two parties.
2. The participants in the collective bargaining of each party are decided by that party.

In case the employee’s party includes many representative organizations participating in collective bargaining as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 68 herein, the representative organization has the right to request collective bargaining shall decide on the number of representatives of each representative organization to participate in the collective bargaining.

In case the employee’s party includes many representative organizations participating in collective bargaining as prescribed in Clause 3, Article 68 herein, the number of representatives of each organization shall be agreed upon by such organizations. In case no agreement is reached, each organization shall determine the number of participating representatives according to the number of its members in proportion to the total number of members of the organizations.

3. Each party is entitled to invite its superior representative organization to send participants acting as the representatives for collective bargaining and the other party must not refuse. The number of collective bargaining representatives of each party shall not exceed the amount specified in Clause 1 of this Article, unless otherwise agreed by the other party.
Article 70. Process of collective bargaining

1. At the request for collective bargaining of an grassroots-level employees’ representative organization which is entitled to request collective bargaining according to Article 68 herein or at the request of the employer, the party receiving the request must not refuse the collective bargaining.
Within 07 working days after receiving the request and the issues for collective bargaining, the parties shall agree on the venue and time for starting the collective bargaining.
The employer is responsible for arranging the time, venue and necessary facilities for the collective bargaining meeting.
The time for starting the collective bargaining shall not exceed 30 days from the date of receipt of the request for collective bargaining.
2. The duration of collective bargaining shall not exceed 90 days from the commencement of the collective bargaining meeting, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.

The period during which the employees’ representatives participate in the collective bargaining meeting shall be considered as the paid working period. In case an employee is a member of the employees’ representative organization attending the collective bargaining meeting, the period during which the employee attends the meeting shall not be included in the period as specified in Clause 2 of Article 176 herein.

3. In the course of collective bargaining, at the request of the employee's representative party, within 10 days after receiving the request, the employer shall provide information on business, production and other issues directly related to the collective bargaining within the enterprise in order to create favorable conditions for collective bargaining, except for information on business secrets and technical secrets of the employer.

4. The grassroots-level employees’ representative organization has the right to organize discussions and collect opinions of employees on the issues, methods of implementation and results of the collective bargaining.

The grassroots-level employees’ representative organization shall decide on the time, venue and method of conducting discussions and collecting opinions of the employees but must not affect the normal production and business activities of the enterprise.
The employer must not cause difficulties, obstruct or interfere with the process of discussing and collecting opinions of employees of the employees’ representative organization.

5. Collective bargaining meetings must be recorded in minutes which must specify issues that have been agreed upon by the two parties and issues on which opinions remain divergent. Minutes of collective bargaining meetings must be signed by representatives of the parties and the preparer of the minutes. The grassroots-level employees’ representative organization shall publicly announce the minutes of collective bargaining meeting to all the employees.
Article 71. Failure of collective bargaining
1. Collective bargaining fails in one of the following cases:
a) A party refuses to negotiate or does not conduct collective bargaining within the time limit specified in Clause 1, Article 70 herein;
b) The parties fail to reach an agreement after the time limit prescribed in Clause 2 Article 70 herein;
c) The time limit prescribed in Clause 2, Article 70 herein has not expired but the parties have mutually determined and declared that the collective bargaining has failed to reach an agreement.

2. In case the negotiation fails, either party shall carry out the procedures for labor dispute settlement in accordance with this Code. When labor disputes are being settled, the employees’ representative organization must not organize a strike.
Article 72. Sectoral collective bargaining and multi-enterprise collective bargaining
1. Principles and issues of sectoral collective bargaining and multi-enterprise collective bargaining shall comply with Articles 66 and 67 herein.

2. The process of sectoral collective bargaining and multi-enterprise collective bargaining shall be decided by the parties, including the agreement to conduct collective bargaining via a collective bargaining council under Article 73 herein.
3. The sectoral collective bargaining shall be decided by the sectoral trade union and the sectoral-level employees’ representative organization.
The multi-enterprise collective bargaining shall be decided by the participating parties in a voluntary and unanimous manner.
Article 73. Multi-enterprise collective bargaining conducted by a collective bargaining council

1. Since consensus reached, the participating parties in multi-enterprise collective bargaining may request the provincial-level People's Committee of the locality where the participating enterprises are headquartered, or of the place chosen by the parties if the participating enterprises have their headquarters located in various provinces and municipalities, to set up a collective bargaining council to conduct collective bargaining.

2. At the requests of the participating parties to multi-enterprise collective bargaining, the provincial-level People's Committee shall decide to set up a collective bargaining council to conduct collective bargaining. The members of such council are:
a) Chairman of the Council, who is appointed by the parties and is responsible for coordinating the activities of the council and supporting the collective bargaining of the parties;
b) Representatives of the participating parties, who are appointed by each party; the number of the representatives in the council shall be agreed by the parties;
c) Representatives of provincial-level People's Committees.
3. The collective bargaining council conducts bargaining at the request of the parties and terminates its operation when a multi-enterprise collective labor agreement is reached by the parties.
4. The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall define the functions, tasks and activities of collective bargaining councils.
Article 74. Responsibilities of the provincial-level People's Committee in collective bargaining
1. To organize training and retraining in collective bargaining skills for participating parties.
2. To elaborate and provide information and data related to socio-economic issues, labor markets and industrial relations to support and promote collective bargaining.

3. To assist the collective bargaining parties to reach an agreement in the process of collective bargaining proactively or at request of both parties; in case of no request, the active support of the provincial-level People's Committee shall only be given if the parties agree.
4. To set up a collective bargaining council at the request of multi-enterprise collective bargaining parties as prescribed in Article 73 herein.
Section 3.
COLLECTIVE LABOR AGREEMENTS
Article 75. Collective labor agreements
1. Collective labor agreement is a written agreement reached through collective bargaining and signed by the parties.

Collective labor agreements include enterprise-level collective labor agreement, sectoral-level collective labor agreement, collective labor agreement with many enterprises and other types of collective labor agreement.
2. The contents of a collective labor agreement must not be against the labor law and must be more favorable for the employees than what is provided by law.
Article 76. Collecting comments and signing of a collective labor agreement

1. With regard to the enterprise collective labor agreement, the draft collective labor agreement negotiated by the parties must be consulted by all employees in the enterprise before signing. An enterprise collective labor agreement shall only be signed when there are more than 50% of the employees of the enterprise voted for voting agree.

2. In the case of collective bargaining agreements, the branches and subjects to collect opinions include all members of the management board of the representative organizations of workers at the enterprises participating in the negotiation. The sector collective labor agreement can only be signed when there are more than 50% of the total number of people voted for voting agree.

For collective bargaining agreements with multiple enterprises, the subjects to collect comments include all employees at the enterprises participating in the bargaining or all members of the management board of the representative organizations of workers at the businesses involved in negotiations. Only enterprises with more than 50% of the people voting for approval can join the signing of a collective labor agreement with multiple businesses.

3. Time, place and method of collecting voting ideas on the draft collective labor agreement shall be decided by the workers' representative organization but must not affect the production and business activities of organizations in negotiation. The employer must not cause difficulties, obstruct or interfere with the process of organizing representatives of employees to vote on the draft agreement.
4. The collective labor agreement is signed by the legal representative of the negotiating parties.

In case a collective labor agreement has multiple enterprises conducted through a collective bargaining council, it shall be signed by the chairman of the collective bargaining council and the legal representative of the negotiating parties.

5. Collective labor agreements must be sent to each contracting party and to the labor specialized agencies of the provincial-level People's Committees according to the provisions of Article 77 of this Code.

For a sectoral-level collective labor agreement or a collective labor agreement with many enterprises, each employer and each representative organization of employees at the enterprises participating in the agreement must receive 01 copy.
6. After the collective labor agreement is signed, the employer must disclose to his employees.
7. The Government shall detail this Article.
Article 77. Sending of the collective labor agreement

Within 10 days from the date the collective labor agreement is signed, the employer participating in the agreement must send 01 copy of the collective labor agreement to the labor agency under the Provincial People's Committee, where the head office is located.
Article 78. Validity and duration of collective labor agreements

1. The effective date of the collective labor agreement is agreed upon by the parties and stated in the agreement. In case the parties do not agree on the effective date, the collective labor agreement takes effect from the signing date.
Collective labor agreements after being effective must be respectfully implement by the parties.

2. The enterprise collective labor agreement takes effect on the employer and all employees of the enterprise. The sector collective labor agreement and the collective labor agreement with many enterprises shall be valid for all employers and employees of enterprises participating in the collective labor agreement.

3. The collective labor agreement has a term of between 01 year and 03 years. The specific period of time shall be agreed upon by the parties and stated in the collective labor agreement. The parties shall have the right to agree on different terms for the contents of a collective labor agreement.
Article 79. Implementation of collective labor agreements at enterprises

1. Employers and employees, including employees who come to work after the effective date of a collective labor agreement, shall be obliged to fully implement the effective collective labor agreement.

2. Where the rights, obligations, and interests of the parties to a labor contract concluded before the effective date of the collective labor agreement are lower than the relevant provisions of the collective labor agreement then provisions of the collective labor agreement shall prevail. The employer's regulations which are not in accordance with the collective labor agreement must be amended accordingly. In the time of the amendment, the relevant content of the collective labor agreement shall apply.

3. When one party considers that the other party has not fully implemented or violated the collective labor agreement, such party shall have the right to request the proper implementation of the collective labor agreement and the parties are responsible for considering and settling. If it is not resolved, each party shall have the right to request the settlement of collective labor disputes in accordance with the law.

Article 80. Implementation of enterprise collective labor agreements in case of division, separation, consolidation or merger; sale, lease, conversion of business type; transfer of ownership, right to use assets of the enterprise

1. In cases of division, splitting, consolidation or merger; sale, lease, conversion of business type; transfer of the ownership or right to use the property of the enterprise, the next employer and the representative organization of the employee have the right to negotiate in accordance with Article 68 of this Code based on the utilization plan, with regard to considering the option of continuing to implement, amend and supplement the old enterprise collective labor agreement or negotiate to sign a new collective labor agreement.

2. In case the enterprise collective labor agreement ceases to be effective due to the termination of operation by the employer, the employee's interests shall be settled according to the provisions of law.
Article 81. Relationship between enterprise collective labor agreements, sectoral-level collective bargaining agreements, and collective enterprise agreements

1. In cases where an enterprise collective labor agreement or a collective labor agreement contains multiple enterprises and a collective labor agreement stipulating different rights, obligations, and interests of employees, it must be implemented according to the content that is most beneficial to the employees.

2. Enterprises subject to the application of a sectoral collective labor agreement or a collective labor agreement with multiple enterprises but have not yet had a collective labor agreement may formulate a collective labor agreement businesses with content that are more beneficial to workers than industry collective bargaining agreements or collective labor agreements with many businesses.

3. To encourage enterprises that have not yet elaborated the sectoral collective bargaining agreement or the collective bargaining agreement to have more enterprises implementing content that is more beneficial to employees of the sectoral collective labor agreement or labor agreement collective action that has multiple businesses.
Article 82. Amendments and supplements to collective labor agreements
1. Collective labor agreements may be amended and supplemented only by voluntary agreements of the parties through collective bargaining.
The amendment and supplementation of the collective labor agreement are done as the negotiation and signing of the collective labor agreement.

2. When the provisions of law change resulting in a collective labor agreement that is no longer in accordance with the provisions of law, the parties must proceed to amend and supplement the collective labor agreement to suit provisions of law. During the period of amendment and supplementation of the collective labor agreement, the rights of the employee shall be implemented in accordance with the law.
Article 83. Collective labor agreement expires

Within 90 days before the expiration of a collective labor agreement, the parties may negotiate to extend the term of the collective labor agreement or sign a new collective labor agreement. In case the parties agree to extend the term of the collective labor agreement, they must seek comments as prescribed in Article 76 of this Code.

When the collective bargaining agreement expires and the parties continue to negotiate, the old collective labor agreement may continue to be implemented for a period not exceeding 90 days from the date the collective labor agreement expires, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.
Article 84. Extending the scope of application of a sector collective labor agreement or a collective labor agreement with many enterprises

1.
