When a sectoral collective bargaining agreement or collective bargaining agreement has many enterprises, the scope of application shall account for over 75% of the employees or over 75% of enterprises of the same industry, line or field in the industrial park, an economic zone, an export processing zone, or a high-tech park, the employer or its representative organization shall request the competent state agency to decide to expand the scope of partial application or the entire agreement with enterprises of the same industry, industry, and sector in industrial parks, economic zones, export processing zones, and hi-tech parks.

2. The Government shall detail Clause 1 of this Article; stipulate the order, procedures, and competence to decide to expand the scope of application of a collective labor agreement prescribed in Clause 1 of this Article.
Article 85. Joining and withdrawing from a sector collective labor agreement or collective labor agreement with many enterprises

1. An enterprise may join a sectoral collective labor agreement, a collective labor agreement with many enterprises with the consent of all employers and the representative organization of employees at the enterprise which is a member of the agreement, except for the case specified in Clause 1, Article 84 of this Code.

2. A member enterprise of a sectoral collective labor agreement having multiple businesses can withdraw from the collective labor agreement when having the consent of all employers and organizations, representatives of employees at the enterprise are members of the agreement, except for cases of special difficulties in production and business activities.
3. The Government shall detail this Article.
Article 86. Invalid collective labor agreement
1. Collective labor agreement is partially invalid when one or some of the contents of the collective labor agreement violates the law.
2. The collective labor agreement is totally invalidated in one of the following cases:
a) All contents of the collective labor agreement violate the law;
b) The signer is not under the authority;
c) Failure to comply with the process of negotiation and signing of the collective labor agreement.
Article 87. Competence to declare a collective bargaining agreement is invalid
The People's Court shall have the right to declare a collective bargaining agreement invalid.
Article 88. Handling of invalid collective labor agreements

When a collective bargaining agreement is declared invalid, the rights, obligations, and interests of the parties stated in the collective labor agreement corresponding to all or part of the declared invalid shall be settled in accordance with the provisions of laws and legal agreements in the labor contract.
Article 89. Expenses for negotiating and signing collective labor agreements
All expenses for negotiating, signing, amending, supplementing, sending and announcing the collective labor agreement are paid by the employer.
Chapter VI
WAGE
Article 90. Wages
1. Wage means the amount of money the employer pays to the employee under an agreement to perform the job, including the wage based on the job or title, wage allowance and other additional payments.
2. The wage according to the job or title cannot be lower than the minimum wage.
3. Employers must ensure equal pay, regardless of gender, for employees of equal value.
Article 91. Minimum wage

1. The minimum wage is the lowest wage paid to employees who perform the simplest jobs under normal working conditions in order to ensure the minimum living standards of employees and their families, in accordance with social and economic development conditions.
2. The minimum wage is set by region, decided by month and hour.

3. The minimum wage is adjusted based on the minimum living standard of workers and their families; the correlation between the minimum wage and the market wage; consumer price index, economic growth rate; labor supply and demand relations; employment and unemployment; labor productivity; affordability of the business.
4. The Government shall detail this Article; decide and publish the minimum wage based on recommendations of the National Wage Council.
Article 92. National Wages Council
1. The National Wage Council is an agency that advises the Government on minimum wages and wage policies for employees.

2. The Prime Minister shall set up a National Wages Council comprising members who are representatives of the Ministry of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs, the Vietnam General Confederation of Labor, a number of user representative organizations for central workers and independent experts.
3. The Government shall specify the functions, tasks, organizational structure and operation of the National Wage Council.
Article 93. Formulation of wage scales, payroll and labor norms

1. The employer must establish a wage scale, payroll, and labor norms as a basis for recruiting and employing employees, agree upon a wage according to the job or title stated in the labor contract and pay wage for employees.
2. The labor level must be the average to ensure that a majority of workers can perform the job without having to extend normal working hours and must finish before official issuance.

3. The employer must consult the representative organization of the employee at the grassroots level for the place where the labor representative organization at the grassroots level is formulated when setting the wage scale, payroll, and labor norms.
Wage scale, payroll and labor rates must be publicly announced at the workplace before implementation.
Article 94. Wage payment principles
1. The employer must pay employees directly, fully and on time. In case the employee cannot receive wage directly, the employer may pay the wage to the one the employee legally authorizes.

2. The employer must not restrict or interfere with the employee's right to self-determination of wage payment. It is forbidden to force employees to spend wages on the purchase of goods or services of the employer or other units designated by the employer.
Article 95. Wage payment
1. Employers pay employees based on agreed wages, labor productivity and quality of job performance.
2. Wages stated in labor contracts and wages paid to employees in Vietnam dong, in case foreign employees in Vietnam may be in foreign currencies.
3. Each time of payment, the employer must notify the payroll list to the employee, clearly stating his/her wage, overtime pay, night work wage, content and amount deducted (if any).
Article 96. Forms of payment
1. The employer and the employee agree on the method of payment based on time, product or package.
2. Wages are paid in cash or through the employees' personal accounts opened at banks.
In case of payment of salaries through an employee's personal account opened at a bank, the employer must pay all fees related to account opening and wage transfer.
3. The Government shall detail this Article.
Article 97. Term of wage payment

1. Employees entitled to hourly, daily or weekly wages shall be paid after the working hours, days, weeks or gross payment shall be agreed upon by the two parties but must not be paid in a lump sum for more than 15 days.
2. The employee who receives a monthly wage is paid once a month or once every half a month. The time of payment is agreed upon by the two parties and must be set at a cyclical time.

3. Employees enjoying wages according to product or piece rate shall be paid according to the agreement of the two parties. If the job has to be worked for many months, the monthly wage will be advanced according to the amount of work done in the month.

4. Where due to force majeure reasons, the employer has sought all remedies but cannot pay the wage on time, it must not be later than 30 days. If the employer pays a late wage of 15 days or more, the employer must compensate the employee for an amount of at least equal to the interest of the deferred payment calculated according to the one-month deposit interest rate due to the bank where the employer opens the payroll account for the employee announced at the time of pay.
Article 98. Wage for overtime pay work and night work
1. An employee who performs overtime work must be paid according to the wage unit or wage for his/her current job as follows:
a) On normal days, at least equal to 150%;
b) On weekends, at least equal to 200%;

c) On public holidays, Lunar New Year Holidays and paid leave days, at least equal to 300%, excluding the wage for public holidays, Lunar New Year Holidays and paid leave days of employees who receive daily wages.

2. An employee who performs night work must be paid with an additional amount at least equal to 30% of the wage calculated according to the wage unit or the wage for a job performed during normal workdays.

3. An employee who performs overtime work at night must be paid under Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article. He/she must be paid with an additional amount equal to 20% of the wage calculated according to the wage unit or the wage for a job performed during daytime of normal workdays, weekends or public holidays, Lunar New Year Holidays.
4. The Government shall detail this Article.
Article 99. Wage in case of work suspension
In case an employee has to suspend working, he/she shall be paid as follows:
1. If due to the fault of the employer, the employee shall be entitled to payment of the full wage according to the labor contract;

2. If due to his/her fault, he/she shall not be entitled to payment of wage; other employees in the same unit who also have to suspend the work shall be entitled to the wages as agreed upon by the two parties, provided that those wages are not lower than the regional minimum wage;

3. If due to power or water incidents rather than the fault of the employer, employees or for other objective reasons such as natural calamity, fire, dangerous epidemic, enemy sabotage, relocation of the operation place upon request of a competent state agency, or for economic reasons, the wage for work suspension must be agreed by the two parties as follows:
a) In case of work suspension for 14 working days or less, the wage for work suspension shall be agreed by the two parties but shall not be lower than the minimum wage;

b) In case of work suspension for more than 14 working days, the wage for work suspension shall be agreed by the two parties but shall ensure that the wage in the first 14 days is not lower than the minimum wage.
Article 100. Payment of wage via foreman

1. In case foremen or similar intermediary persons are used, the employer who is the principal owner shall have a list and addresses of these people together with a list of employees working with them, and shall ensure that they comply with the law on wage payment and occupational safety and hygiene.

2. In case a foreman or similar intermediary person fails to pay wages or pays insufficient wages and fails to ensure other interests of employees, the employer who is the principal owner shall pay wages to, and to ensure such interests of, the employees.

In this case, the employer who is the principal owner shall have the right to request compensation from the foreman or similar intermediary person, or request a competent state agency to resolve the dispute in accordance with law.
Article 101. Advance of wage
1. An employee shall be given a wage in advance according to the conditions agreed upon by the two parties.

2. An employer shall advance a wage amount to an employee corresponding to the number of days off which the employee takes to perform citizens’ obligations from 01 week to 01 month at most according to the labor contract and the employee shall refund this advance amount.
The employee who is enlisted in the army in accordance with the Law on Military Service shall not be entitled to an advance of wage.
3. When taking annual leave, an employee is entitled to an advance payment of at least equal to the wage of days off.
Article 102. Deduction of wages
1. An employer may only make deductions from the wage of an employee for compensation for damage of the employer’s tools, equipment and assets in accordance with Article 129 of this Code.
2. The employee shall be entitled to know the reasons for his/her wage deductions.
3. A monthly wage deduction must not exceed 30% of the monthly wage of an employee after having paid compulsory social insurance, health insurance and unemployment and personal income tax.
Article 103. Wage raise, rank promotion, allowances and subsidies

Wage raise, rank promotion, allowances, subsidies and other incentives for employees must be agreed in the labor contracts and the collective labor agreement or stipulated in the regulations of the employer.
Article 104. Bonuses
1. Bonus is a sum of money or property or other forms that an employer rewards his/her employees on the basis of annual business results and the level of work performance of employees.

2. Bonus regulations shall be decided and publicly announced by the employer at the workplace after consultation with the representative organization of the grassroots-level employees in the case there is a representative organization of the grassroots-level employees.
Chapter VII
WORKING TIME AND REST TIME
Section 1
WORKING TIME
Article 105. Normal working time
1. Normal working time shall not exceed 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week.

2. An employer may determine the working time on an hourly, daily or weekly basis but must notify his/her employees; in case of working on a weekly basis, the normal working time shall not exceed 10 hours per day and not exceed 48 hours per week.
The State encourages employers to apply 40 working hours per week for employees.
3. An employer shall ensure the working time limit for employees who are exposed to dangerous and harmful factors in accordance with national technical regulations and relevant laws.
Article 106. Working hours at night
Working hours at night are counted from 22:00 pm on the previous day to 06:00 am on the next day.
Article 107. Overtime work
1. Overtime is time worked in addition to normal working hours prescribed in the law, collective labor agreements or internal working regulations
2. An employer may request an employee to work overtime upon fully meeting the following conditions:
a) Obtaining the employee’s consent;

b) Ensuring that the number of overtime working hours of the employee does not exceed 50% of the normal working hours per day; in case of applying regulations on weekly work, the total of normal working hours and overtime working hours must not exceed 12 hours per day; does not exceed 40 hours per month;
c) Ensuring that the number of overtime working hours of the employee does not exceed 200 hours per year, except for the case specified in Clause 3 of this Article.
3. An employer may request an employee to work overtime for no more than 300 hours per year in the following industries, jobs or cases:
a) Producing, processing and exporting textile, garment, leather, shoes, electric and electronic products; processing agricultural, forestry, salt-producing and aquatic products;
b) Producing, supplying electricity, telecommunications, oil refining; water supply and drainage;
c) In case of handling jobs requiring employees with high professional and technical qualifications which labor market can not provide sufficient and timely;

d) In case of urgent work that cannot be delayed, due to the seasonality and timing of raw materials, products or to solve jobs arising due to unpredictable objective factors result from weather consequences, natural disasters, enemy sabotage, fire, lack of electricity, lack of raw materials and technical problems of production lines;
dd) Other cases prescribed by the Government.
4. If an employer organizes the overtime working as prescribed in Clause 3 of this Article, he/she shall send a written notification to the labor agency of the provincial People's Committee.
5. The Government shall detail this Article.
Article 108. Working overtime in special cases

An employer may request an employee to work overtime in any days without limitation on the number of overtime hours as prescribed in Article 107 of this Code and the employee may not refuse in the following cases:
1. Implementing a call-up or mobilization in order to ensure national defense or security as prescribed by law;

2. Implementing the tasks to protect human lives and assets of agencies, organizations or individuals in the prevention and remediation of consequences of a natural calamity, fire, dangerous epidemic or disaster, except for the case that may affect the employee’s health and lives in accordance with the law on occupational safety and hygiene.
Section 2
REST TIME
Article 109. Rest breaks during working hours

1. An employee who works for more than 06 hours per day under Article 105 of this Code shall be entitled to a break of at least 30 minutes in the middle of working. If working at night, he/she shall be entitled to a break of at least 45 minutes in the middle of working.
In case an employee works in a continuous shift of 06 hours or more, the break time shall be counted into working hours.
2. Besides the breaks in the middle of working prescribed in Clauses 1 of this Article, the employer shall determine other short breaks and include them in the internal working regulations.
Article 110. Breaks between shifts
An employee who works in shifts shall be entitled to a break of at least 12 hours before moving to another shift.
Article 111. Weekly breaks

1. Every week, an employee shall be entitled to a break of at least 24 consecutive hours. In case it is impossible for an employee to have a weekly break due to the cycle of work, the employer shall ensure the employee have at least 4 days off on average in a month.
2. An employer may determine and schedule weekly breaks either on Sunday or another fixed weekday but shall include them in the internal working regulations.

3. In case weekly days off coincide with public holidays and New Year holidays specified in Clause 1, Article 112 of this Code, employees shall be entitled to a weekly day off on the next working day.
Article 112. Public and New Year holidays
1. Employees are entitled to a leave of absence from work and full pay during the following holidays:
a) Calendar New Year Holiday: 01 day (the first day of January of the calendar year);
b) Lunar New Year Holidays: 05 days;
c) Liberation Day: 01 day (April 30 of the solar calendar);
d) International Labor Day: 01 day (the first day of May of each calendar year);
dd) National Day: 02 days (the second day of September of each calendar year and 01 day immediately preceding or after);
e) Commemorative Celebration of Vietnam’s Forefather - Kings Hung: 01 day (the tenth of March of the lunar year).

2. An foreign employee working in Vietnam, in addition to the public holidays specified in Clause 1 of this Article, he/she shall be entitled to 01 traditional new year holiday and 01 national day of his/her country.
3. Annually, on the basis of practical conditions, the Prime Minister shall decide on specific holidays prescribed at Points b and dd, Clause 1 of this Article.
Article 113. Annual leave
1. An employee who has been working for an employer for full 12 months shall be entitled a fully paid annual leave as stated in his/her labor contract as follows:
a) 12 working days for an employee working in normal conditions;
b) 14 working days for a juvenile employee, a disabled employee or an employee doing a heavy, hazardous and dangerous job;
c) 16 working days for an employee doing an extremely heavy, hazardous or dangerous job.
2. An employee who has been working less than 12 months for an employer shall be entitled to take annual leave with the number of leave days proportionate to the working time.
3. An employee who, due to job leaving or job loss, fails to take or fully take his/her annual leave shall be entitled to a cash payment for the untaken leave days.

4. An employer shall be responsible for setting the annual leave schedule after consulting with employees and must notify it in advance to them. An employee may reach an agreement with the employer on taking annual leave in installments or combining annual leaves of maximum every three years.
5. When taking annual leave before the period of payment, an employee shall be entitled to an advance payment in accordance with Clause 3, Article 101 of this Code.

6. When taking annual leave, if an employee travels by road, railway or waterway and the return trip takes more than 02 days, the travel days from the 3rd day onward will be added to the annual leave and this will be applied for only one annual leave in a year.
7. The Government shall detail this article.
Article 114. Annual leave increased based on the length of employment
The annual leave of an employee stipulated in Clause 1, Article 113 of this Code will be increased 1 day for every 05 years’ working for an employer.
Article 115. Personal leave and unpaid leave
1. An employee may take fully paid leave for personal reasons and must notify the employer in the following cases:
a) Marriage: take 03 days;
b) Marriage of his/her child: 01 day;
c) Death of a blood parent, an adoptive parent, a blood parent of his/her spouse, an adoptive parent of his/her spouse, his/her spouse or child: 03 days.

2. An employee may take a day off without pay and shall inform the employer when a paternal or maternal grandparent or blood sibling dies; his/her father or mother gets married; or a blood sibling gets married.
3. An employee may agree with the employer on unpaid leave in addition to the leaves specified in Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article.
Section 3
WORKING TIME AND REST TIME FOR PEOPLE DOING SPECIAL JOBS
Article 116. Working time, rest time for persons doing special jobs

For special jobs in the field of road, railway, waterway or airway transportation; petroleum prospecting and exploitation at sea; working at sea; offshore work; arts; use of radiation and nuclear techniques; application of high-frequency waves; informatics and information technology; research and application of advanced science and technology; industrial design; diver's jobs; work in pit mines; seasonal production work and processing of goods under orders; and work that requires 24/24 hours on duty; For other special jobs as stipulated by the Government, the managing ministries and branches shall specify working time and rest time after consulting the Ministry of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs and ensure compliance with Article 109 of this Code.
Chapter VIII
LABOR DISCIPLINE AND MATERIAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Section 1
LABOR DISCIPLINE
Article 117. Labor discipline

Labor discipline means regulations on compliance with time requirements, technology and production and business administration issued by the employer in the internal working regulations and prescribed by law.
Article 118. Internal working regulations
1. An employer employing 10 or more employees must have internal working regulations in writing.
2. The contents of internal working regulations must not be contrary to the labor law and other relevant laws. The internal working regulations contain the following principal contents:
a) Working time and rest time;
b) Order at workplace;
c) Occupational safety and hygiene at workplace;
d) Prevention and combat against sexual harassment at the workplace; order and procedures for handling sexual harassment at the workplace;
dd) Protection of assets and technological and business secrets and intellectual property of the employer;
f) Temporary transfer of employees to other jobs other than jobs stipulated in the labor contract;
g) Employees’ violations of labor discipline, forms of dealing with violations of labor discipline;
h) Material responsibility;
i) Persons competent to handle violations of labor discipline.

3. Before issuing the internal working regulations or amending and supplementing the internal working regulations, an employer shall consult the representative organization of the grassroots-level employees in the case there is a representative organization of the grassroots-level employees.
4. The internal working regulations must be notified to employees and their key contents must be displayed at necessary places in the workplace.
5. The Government shall detail this Article.
Article 119. Registration of internal working regulations
1. An employer employing 10 or more employees shall register its internal working regulations with a labor agency under the provincial People's Committee where the employer registers its business.
2. Within 10 days from the date of issuance of the internal working regulations, an employer shall submit a dossier for registration of the internal working regulations.

3. Within 07 working days from the date of receipt of a dossier for registration of the internal working regulations, if the internal working regulations have contents contrary to law, the labor agency under the provincial People's Committee shall notify and instruct the employer to amend, supplement and re-register.

4. In case an employer has branches, units, production and business establishments located in different areas, he/she shall send the registered internal working regulations to the labor agency under the provincial People's Committee where the branches, units and production and business establishments are located.

5. Based on specific conditions, the labor agency under the provincial-level People's Committee may authorize the labor agency of the district-level People's Committee to register internal working regulations under this Article.
Article 120. Dossier for registration of internal working regulations
An application for registration of internal labor regulations includes:
1. An application for registration of the internal working regulations;
2. The internal working regulations;
3. Minutes of comments of the representative organization of the grassroots-level employees in the case there is a representative organization of the grassroots-level employees;
4. Documents of the employer related to labor discipline and material responsibilities (if any).
Article 121. Validity of internal working regulations

The internal working regulations shall be effective 15 days after the date the competent state agency prescribed in Article 119 of this Code receives the sufficient registration dossier of the internal working regulations.
In case the employer employing less than 10 employees issues internal working regulations in writing, the validity shall be decided by the employer in the internal working regulations.
Article 122. Principles, order and procedures for handling violations of labor discipline
1. The handling of a violation of labor discipline is provided as follows:
a) The employer must prove the employee's fault;
b) The representative organization of the grassroots-level employees where the employee being disciplined is a member must participate in the handling;

c) The employee must be present and may defend himself/herself or ask a lawyer or a representative organization of employees to defend him/her; if the employee is under 15 years old, his/her at-law representative must participate in the handling;
d) The handling of the violation of labor discipline must be recorded in the minutes.
2. It shall be prohibited to impose more than one form of discipline for a single violation of labor discipline.

3. In case an employee simultaneously commits more than one violation of labor discipline, it shall be only allowed to apply the highest form of discipline corresponding to the most serious violation.
4. Labor discipline may not be imposed for violations committed by an employee who is currently:
a) Taking sickness or convalescence leave or a leave with the employer’s consent;
b) Kept in custody or temporary detention;
c) Waiting for results of verification and conclusion of a competent agency for acts of violation specified in Clauses 1 and 2, Article 125 of this Code;
d) A pregnant female employee; an employee taking maternity leave or rearing a child under 12 months of age.

5. Labor discipline shall not be imposed on an employee who violates the internal working regulations while suffering a mental disorder or another disease which deprives him/her of the capacity to perceive or control his/her acts.
6. The Government shall specify the order and procedures for handling of violations of labor discipline.
Article 123. Statute of limitations for handling violations of labor discipline

1. The statute of limitations for handling a violation of labor discipline is 6 months from the date the violation is committed. The statute of limitations for handling a violation of labor discipline directly related to finance and assets or disclosure of technological or business secrets is 12 months.

2. Upon expiry of the period specified in Clause 4, Article 122 of this Code, if the statute of limitations for handling violations of labor discipline has expired or still remained valid but less than 60 days, it may be extended to handle violations of labor discipline but for no more than 60 days from the expiry date mentioned above.
3. The employer shall issue a decision on handle violations of labor discipline within the time limits specified in Clauses 1 and 2 of this Article.
Article 124. Forms of handling of violations of labor discipline
1. Reprimand.
2. Prolongation of the wage rise period for no more than 06 months.
3. Demotion.
4. Dismissal.
Article 125. Application of dismissal as a form of discipline
Dismissal may be applied by an employer as a form of discipline in the following cases:
1. An employee commits an act of theft, embezzlement, gambling, intentional infliction of injury, use of drugs inside the workplace;

2. An employee commits an act of disclosing technological or business secrets or causing serious damage or threatening to cause serious damage to the assets or interests of the employer; sexual harassment at the workplace as stipulated in the internal working regulations;

3. An employee who has been subject to the disciplinary measure of prolonging the wage rise period or dismissing commits recidivism when the disciplinary record has not yet been written off. Recidivism means that an employee re-commits the same violation for which he/she has been disciplined while his/her disciplinary record has not yet been written off as prescribed in Article 126 of this Code;
4. An employee has been absent from work without permission for a total of 05 working days within 30 days or 20 days within 365 days without plausible reasons.

Plausible reasons include natural disaster, fire, illness of the employee or his/her next of kin with certification by a competent health treatment and examination establishment and other events defined in the internal working regulations.
Article 126. Writing off of disciplinary records, reduction of the duration of labor discipline

1. After 03 months from the date of being reprimanded or after 06 months from the date of being disciplined by prolonging the wage rise period or after 03 years from the date of being disciplined for dismissal, if an employee does not commit recidivism, his/her disciplinary record be automatically written off.

2. An employee who is subject to the disciplinary measure of prolonging the wage rise period and has served half of the duration of the discipline may be considered by the employer for a reduction of such duration if showing progress.
Article 127. Prohibited acts when handling violations of labor discipline
1. Infringing upon the employees' health, honor, life, prestige and dignity.
2. Applying a fine or wage reduction instead of a disciplinary measure.
3. Disciplining an employee who has committed a violation which is not defined in the internal working regulations or not agreed upon in signed the labor contract or not prescribed in the labor code.
Article 128. Work suspension

1. An employer may suspend an employee from working if the employer considers that the case of violation is complex and any continued performance of the work by the employee can cause difficulties to verification work. Work suspension may only be applied after having consulting the representative organization of the grassroots-level employees where the employee under consideration for suspension is a member.

2. The period of work suspension must not exceed 15 days, or 90 days in special cases. During the period of work suspension, the employee shall be entitled to 50 per cent of the wage he/she receives prior to the suspension.
Upon the expiry of the period of work suspension, the employer must receive the employee back to his/her work.
3. In case the employee is disciplined, he/she is not required to reimburse the wage advanced to him/her.
4. In case the employee is not disciplined, the employer shall pay the full wage for the period of work suspension.
Section 2
MATERIAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 129. Compensation for damage
1. An employee who causes damage to tools and equipment or the assets of the employer shall pay compensation in accordance with law or the employer’s internal working regulations.

In case due to negligence an employee causes a minor damage valued at no more than 10 months’ regional minimum wage announced by the Government and applied at the employee’s workplace, the employee shall pay compensation of no more than 03 months’ wage which shall be deducted monthly from his/her wage in accordance with Clause 3, Article 102 of this Code.

2. An employee who loses tools, equipment or assets of the employer or other assets assigned to him/her by the employer, or uses supplies in excess of the permitted norms shall compensate the whole or a part of the damage at the market price; in case a contract of responsibility has been signed, the amount of compensation must comply with such contract; in case the damage is caused by a natural disaster, fire, enemy sabotage, epidemic, calamity or another objective event which is unforeseeable and irremediable and every necessary measure has been taken to full ability, no compensation is required.
Article 130. Handling of damage compensation

1. Consideration and decision on the levels of compensation must be based on the fault, the actual level of damage, the actual family conditions, personal records and property of the employee concerned.
2. The Government shall specify the order, procedures and statute of limitations for handling of damage compensation.
Article 131. Complaints about labor discipline and material responsibilities

An employee who is handled for violation of labor discipline, suspended from work, or required to pay compensation in accordance with the regime of material responsibilities and is not satisfied with the handling decision, may file a complaint with the employer or a competent agency as stipulated by law, or request settlement of a labor dispute according to the procedures as stipulated by law.
The Government shall detail this Article.
Chapter IX
OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HYGIENE
Article 132. Compliance with the law on occupational safety and hygiene
Employers, employees, agencies, organizations and individuals related to labor and production shall comply with the law on occupational safety and hygiene.
Article 133. Occupational safety and hygiene program
1. The Government decides the national Program on occupational safety and sanitation.

2. Provincial-level People’s Committees shall submit local occupational safety and hygiene programs to the same-level People Councils for decision, and include them in their socio-economic development plans.
Article 134. Assurance of occupational safety and hygiene at workplace
1. An employer shall assume responsibility for fully implementing measures to ensure occupational safety and hygiene at the workplace.

2. An employee shall assume responsibility for observing the regulations, internal rules, procedures and requirements on occupational safety and hygiene; complying with law and mastering the knowledge and skills of measures to ensure occupational safety and hygiene at the workplace.
Chapter X
SEPARATE PROVISIONS FOR FEMALE EMPLOYEES AND ENSURING GENDER EQUALITY
Article 135. State policies
1. Ensuring the female and male employees’ rights to employment equality, taking measures to ensure gender equality, preventing and combating against sexual harassment at the workplace.
2. Encouraging employers to create conditions for female and male employees to have regular employment, extensively implementing systems of flexible working hours, part-time work or home-based work.

3. Taking measures to create employment opportunities, improve working conditions, raise vocational qualifications and healthcare, and increase material and spiritual welfare for female employees in order to assist them in effectively bringing into play their vocational capacity and harmoniously combining their working lives with family lives.
4. Formulating policies on tax reductions for employers using many female employees in accordance with tax laws.

5. The State shall develop plans and measures to organize crèches and kindergartens in areas with large numbers of employees. Developing various forms of training which are favorable for female employees to acquire standby vocational skills suitable to their physical and physiological characteristics and their motherhood function.
6. The Government shall detail this Article.
Article 136. Responsibilities of employers
1. Ensuring gender equality and implementing measures to promote gender equality in recruitment, employment, training, working time, rest time, wages and other policies.
2. Consulting female employees or their representatives when taking decisions on issues related to the rights and interests of women.
3. Ensuring sufficient bathrooms and appropriate toilets in the workplace.
4. Assisting and supporting in building crèches and kindergartens, or covering part of childcare expenses at crèches and kindergartens incurred by female employees.
Article 137. Protection of maternity for female employees
1. An employer may not mobilize employees to work at night, work overtime or go on a long working trip in the following cases:
a) The employee is in her seventh month of pregnancy, or in her sixth month of pregnancy in case of working in a mountainous, remote, distant, border or island area;
b) The employee is nursing a child under 12 months of age.

2. In case a female employee is engaged in heavy, hazardous, dangerous or extremely heavy, hazardous, dangerous work or work adversely affecting the reproductive and child-rearing function during her pregnancy and notifies the employer, she shall be entitled to be transferred to a lighter and safer work or have her daily working time reduced by 01 hour without any reductions in wages, rights and interests until the end of nursing a child under 12 months of age.

3. An employer may neither dismiss a female employee nor unilaterally terminate the labor contract with a female employee for the reason of her marriage, pregnancy, maternity leave, or that she is nursing a child under 12 months of age, except the case in which the employer is an individual who dies, or is declared by a court to have lost his/her civil act capacity, or to be missing or dead, or the employer is not an individual terminating operation or is notified by a business registration agency of the provincial People's Committee that there is no legal representative, authorized person to exercise the rights and obligations of the legal representative.
In case the employment contract expires while a female employee is pregnant or nursing a child under 12 months of age, a new labor contract shall be given priority.

4. A female employee in her menstruation period shall be entitled to a 30-minute break in every working day; a female employee nursing a child under 12 months of age shall be entitled to a 60-minute break in every working day with full wage as stated in the labor contract.
Article 138. Right of pregnant employees to unilaterally terminate or postpone labor contracts

1. In case a pregnant employee has a certificate of a competent health treatment and examination establishment which states that continued work will adversely affect her pregnancy, she may unilaterally terminate the labor contract or temporarily postpone the performance of the labor contract.

In case of unilaterally terminating the labor contract or temporarily postponing the performance of the labor contract, the employee must send to the employer a notice enclosed with the certificate of a competent health treatment and examination establishment which states that continued work will adversely affect her pregnancy

2. In case of temporarily postponing the performance of the labor contract, the period of postponement shall be agreed upon by the employee with the employer but must be at least equal to the time designated by the competent health examination and treatment establishment. In case there is no designation of the competent health examination and treatment establishment regarding the time of temporary leave, the two parties shall agree on the time of temporarily postponing the performance of the labor contract.
Article 139. Maternity leave
1. A female employee is entitled to 06 months of prenatal and postnatal leave; prenatal leave must not exceed 02 months.
In case a female employee gives birth to twin or more babies, counting from the second child upward, for each child the mother shall be entitled to an extra month of leave.
2. During the maternity leave, a female employee shall be entitled to maternity policies provided by the law on social insurance.
3. After the maternity leave period stipulated in Clause 1 of this Article, if a female employee wishes, she may take additional leave without pay after agreed upon with the employer.

4. Before the expiration of her maternity leave stipulated in Clause 1 of this Article, a female employee may return to work after having taken at leas04 months of maternity leave but she must give advance notice to the employer and agreed by her employer. She also must have a certificate from a competent health treatment and examination establishment that early resumption of work will not adversely affect her health. In this case, the female employee continues to receive the maternity allowance as provided by the law on social insurance, in addition to the wage paid by the employer for her working days.

5. For a male employee when his wife gives birth, an employee who adopts children less than 06 months of age, a female employee who is a surrogate mother and an employee who is a mother requesting surrogacy shall be entitled to take the maternity leave as provided by the law on social insurance
Article 140. Employment guarantee for employees after maternity leave

An employee shall be guaranteed the old employment when she returns to work after taking the maternity leave as provided in Clauses 1, 3 and 5, Article 139 of this Code without any reduction in wages, rights and interests; in case the old employment is no longer available, the employer shall arrange another employment for her with a wage not lower than that paid to her before her maternity leave.
Article 141. Allowances for leave for caring a sick child, for pregnancy checks-up and for applying contraceptive measures

When taking leaves for caring a sick child who is under 07 years of age, pregnancy check-up, miscarriage, abortion, dead or diseased fetus in womb, for applying measures of contraception and sterilization, a female employee shall be entitled to maternity allowance in accordance with the law on social insurance.
Article 142. Occupations and work adversely affecting child bearing and nursing functions
1. The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall promulgate a list of occupations and work that are harmful to child bearing and nursing functions.

2. The employer must provide sufficient information on the work’s dangerous nature, risks and requirements for the employees to choose and must ensure the occupational safety and hygiene conditions for the employees in accordance with regulations when employing them for the work on the list specified in Clause 1 of this Article.
Chapter XI
PRIVACY PROVISIONS FOR LABOR
MINORS AND SOME OTHER EMPLOYEES
Section 1
MINOR EMPLOYEES
Article 143. Minor employees
1. A minor employee is an employee under 18 years of age.
2. Persons aged between full 15 and under 18 may not work or work at workplaces prescribed in Article 147 of this Code.
3. Persons aged between full 13 and under 15 may only perform light jobs according to the list promulgated by the Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs.
4. Persons aged under 13 may only perform the jobs specified in Clause 3, Article 145 of this Code.
Article 144. Principles of employment of minor employees
1. A minor employee may only perform jobs suitable to his/her health to ensure physical, mental and personality development.
2. An employer, when employing minor employees, shall assume the responsibility to take care of employees in terms of labor, health, and study in the labor process.

3. When employing minor employees, an employer must have the consent of their parents or guardians; make a separate monitoring book, record full name, date of birth, current job, results of periodical health checks, and shall present it at the request of a competent state agency.
4. An employer must create opportunities for minor employees to learn cultural, vocational education, train, foster and improve occupational skills qualifications.
Article 145. Use of employees aged under 15 years
1. When employing persons under 15 years of age to work, an employer must comply with the following provisions:
a) To sign a labor contract in writing with a person under 15 years of age and his/her legal representative;
b) To arrange working hours without affecting the learning time of persons under 15 years of age;

c) To have a health certificate issued by a competent health facility certifying the health of persons under 15 years of age suitable to their jobs and to organize periodical health checks at least once every 06 months;
d) To ensure working conditions, occupational safety, and sanitation suitable for ages.
2. An employer shall only recruit and employ persons aged between full 13 and under 15 to perform light jobs as prescribed in Clause 3, Article 143 of this Code.

3. Recruitment and employment of persons aged under 13 years is prohibited, except for art, physical training and sports jobs without prejudice to physical, mental and human development and must have the consent of a labor agency of the provincial-level People's Committee.
4. The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall detail this Article.
Article 146. Working time of minors
1. The working time of persons under 15 years must not exceed 04 hours in 01 day and 20 hours in 01 weeks; and the employer may not employ these minors to work overtime or at night.

2. The working time of a person aged from full 15 to less than 18 must not exceed 08 hours in a day and 40 hours in a week. Persons aged between full 15 and under 18 may work overtime and work at night in a number of occupations and jobs on the list promulgated by the Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs.
Article 147. Prohibited jobs and workplaces for employees aged between full 15 and under 18 years
1. Employment of persons aged between full 15 and under 18 is prohibited in the following jobs:
a) Carrying and lifting heavy objects which are beyond a minor’s physical strength;
b) Producing and trading in alcohol, wine, beer, cigarettes, substances affecting the spirit or other addictive substances;
c) Producing, using or transporting chemicals, gases, explosives;
d) Maintenance of equipment and machinery;
e) Demolition of construction works;
f) Melting, blowing, casting, rolling, molding and welding of metals;
g) Scuba diving, fishing, and offshore fishing;
h) Other jobs that are harmful the physical, mental and personality development of minors.
2. Employment of persons aged full 15 to under 18 years is prohibited in the following workplaces:
a) Underwater, underground, in caves and in tunnels;
b) Construction site;
c) Animal slaughter facilities;
d) Casinos, bars, dance halls, karaoke parlors, hotels, hostels, saunas, massage parlors; lottery business points, electronic game services;
e) Other workplaces which are harmful to the physical, mental and personality development of minor employees.
3. The Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall specify the lists at Point h, Clause 1 and Point dd, Clause 2 of this Article.
Section 2
ELDERLY EMPLOYEES
Article 148. Elderly employees
1. An elderly employee is a person who continues to work after the age prescribed in Clause 2, Article 169 of this Code.
2. Elderly employees shall be entitled to agree with employers on reducing daily working hours or applying part-time working regimes.
3. The State encourages the employment of elderly employees to work in conformity with their health to ensure labor rights and efficient use of human resources.
Article 149. Employment of elderly employees
1. When employing an elderly employee, the two parties may agree to enter into several definite-term labor contracts.

2. When the elderly employee who is enjoying the pension prescribed in the Law on Social Insurance works under a new labor contract, in addition to the benefits he/she is entitled to under the retirement regime, he/she is entitled to the salaries and other benefits in accordance with the law and labor contracts.

3. It is prohibited to employ elderly employees to perform heavy, hazardous, dangerous or extremely heavy, hazardous, dangerous jobs, which adversely affect the health of elderly employees, except for the cases that ensure safe working conditions.
4. Employers shall be responsible for taking care of the health of elderly employees at the workplace.
Section 3
VIETNAMESE EMPLOYEES WORKING ABROAD, EMPLOYEES OF FOREIGN ORGANIZATIONS AND INDIVIDUALS IN VIETNAM, FOREIGN EMPLOYEES WORKING IN VIETNAM
Article 150. Vietnamese employees working abroad, employees of foreign organizations and individuals in Vietnam
1. The State encourages enterprises, agencies, organizations, and individuals to seek and expand the labor market in order to send Vietnamese employees to work abroad.
Vietnamese employees working abroad shall comply with the laws of Vietnam and host countries, unless otherwise provided by treaties to which Vietnam is a contracting party.

2. Vietnamese citizens working for foreign organizations in Vietnam, in industrial parks, economic zones, export processing zones, hi-tech parks or working for individuals who are foreign citizens in Vietnam shall abide by Vietnamese laws and are protected by law.
3. The Government shall detail the recruitment and management of Vietnamese employees working for foreign organizations and individuals in Vietnam.
Article 151. Conditions for foreign citizens to work in Vietnam
1. A foreign citizen working in Vietnam is foreign nationals and must meet the following conditions:
a) Being 18 years of age or older and having full civil act capacity;
b) Having professional qualifications, techniques, work skills, and work experience; have good health as prescribed by the Minister of Health;
c) Not being a person who is serving a penalty or has not had his/her criminal record remitted or is being examined for penal liability in accordance with foreign law or Vietnamese law;
d) Having a work permit granted by a competent Vietnamese state agency, except for the case specified in Article 154 of this Code.

2. The term of a labor contract for foreign citizens working in Vietnam must not exceed the term of the work permit. When employing foreign citizens working in Vietnam, the two parties may agree to enter into several definite-term labor contracts.
3. Foreign citizens working in Vietnam must abide by the Vietnamese labor law and are protected by Vietnamese law, unless otherwise provided by treaties to which Vietnam is a contracting party.
Article 152. Conditions for recruiting and employing foreign employees to work in Vietnam

1. Enterprises, agencies, organizations, individuals, and contractors may only recruit foreign citizens in such positions as manager, managing director, expert and technical employee which Vietnamese employees are still unable to fill to meet production and business requirements.

2. Enterprises, agencies, organizations, and individuals shall, before recruiting foreign citizens to work in the territory of Vietnam, explain their labor demands and obtain written approval of the competent state agencies.

3. Contractors shall, before recruiting and employing foreign citizens to work in the territory of Vietnam, declare in detail the job positions, professional and technical qualifications, working experience and working time that need to use foreign employees to execute the bidding package and obtain the written approval of the competent state agency.
Article 153. Responsibilities of employers and foreign employees
1. Foreign employees must present work permits at the request of competent state agencies.

2. Foreign employees working in Vietnam without a work permit shall be forced to leave Vietnam or be deported in accordance with the law on entry, exit, transit, and residence of foreigners in Vietnam.
3. Employers who employ foreign employees to work for themselves without work permits shall be handled according to the provisions of law.
Article 154. Foreign employees working in Vietnam are not eligible for work permits
1. Being the owner or capital contributing member of a limited liability company with the value of capital contribution under the Government's regulations.
2. Being the Chairman of the Board of Directors or a member of the Board of Directors of a joint-stock company with the value of capital contribution as prescribed by the Government.
3. Being the head of a representative office or project or responsible primarily for the operation of international organizations and foreign non-governmental organizations in Vietnam.
4. Entering Vietnam with a term of less than 03 months to conduct service offerings.

5. Entering Vietnam for less than 03 months to deal with incidents, complicated technical and technological situations that affect or threaten to affect production and business activities of Vietnamese experts and foreign experts currently in Vietnam cannot handle it.
6. Being a foreign lawyer who has been granted a law practice license in Vietnam in accordance with the Law on Lawyers.
7. The cases in accordance with the provisions of international treaties to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is a member.
8. Foreigners marrying Vietnamese and living in the Vietnamese territory.
9. Other cases as prescribed by the Government.
Article 155. Validity duration of work permits
The maximum validity duration of a work permit is 02 years, in case of extension, it can be extended only once for a maximum of 02 years.
Article 156. Cases of termination of validity of work permits
1. The work permit expires.
2. The labor contract terminates.
3. The content of the labor contract is not consistent with the content of the granted work permit.
4. Working not in accordance with the contents of the issued work permit.
5. The contracts in the domains that are the basis for generating work permits which are expired or terminated.
6. There is a written notice of the foreign party quitting the appointment of a foreign employee to work in Vietnam.
7. Enterprises, organizations, partners of the Vietnamese side or foreign organizations in Vietnam employing foreign employees to terminate their operations.
8. The work permit is revoked.
Article 157. Issuance, re-issuance, extension, and revocation of work permits, certifications not subject to work permits

The Government shall stipulate the conditions, order, and procedures for the issuance, re-issuance, extension, and revocation of work permits and certifications not subject to work permits for foreign employees working in Vietnam.
Section 4
DISABLED EMPLOYEES
Article 158. State policies for disabled employees

The State protects the rights to work and to self-employment of disabled persons, and shall formulate policies to encourage and provide incentives for employers to create jobs for and employ disabled persons in accordance with the Law on Persons with Disabilities.
Article 159. Employment of disabled persons
1. An employer shall ensure working conditions, working tools, occupational safety and hygiene, and organize periodical health checks suitable for disabled employees.
2. An employer shall consult disabled employees before deciding on matters involving their rights and interests.
Article 160. Prohibited acts in employment of disabled persons

1. Employing an employee with mild disability who has lost 51% or more of his/her working ability, an employee with severe disability or extremely severe disability to work overtime or at night, except for cases when obtaining the disabled employee’s consents.

2. Employing a disabled employee to perform a heavy, hazardous and dangerous job on the list promulgated by the Minister of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs without the consent of the disabled person after the employer has provided all the information about the job.
Section 5
DOMESTIC EMPLOYEES
Article 161. Domestic employees
1. Domestic employee is a person who regularly does housework for one or more families.
Housework includes cooking, housekeeping, babysitting, caring for sick persons, caring for the elderly, driving, and gardening and other houseworks which are not related to commercial activities.
2. The Government shall prescribe regulations on domestic employees.
Article 162. Labor contracts for domestic employees
1. An employer shall engage in a written labor contract with a domestic employee.
2. The duration of a labor contract for a domestic employee may be negotiated by both parties. Either party may unilaterally terminate the labor contract with an advance notice of 15 days.
3. Both sides shall clearly specify the form of wage payment and the terms of payment, daily working hours and accommodation in the labor contract.
Article 163. Obligations of an employer employing domestic employee(s)
1. To fully implement the agreements in the labor contract.
2. To pay to the domestic employee an amount of his/her social insurance and health insurance as provided by law to enable the employee to self-manage his/her insurance.
3. To respect the honor and dignity of the domestic employee.
4. To provide a clean and hygienic accommodation for the domestic employee if so agreed.
5. To create opportunities for the domestic employee to receive education and vocational training.
6. To pay travel expenses for the domestic employee to return home at the end of his/her service, except the case in which the domestic employee terminates the labor contract ahead of time.
Article 164. Obligations of a domestic employee
1. To fully implement the agreements in the labor contract.
2. To pay compensation as agreed upon or provided by law in case of damaging or losing any property of the employer.
3. To timely notify the employer of any possibilities and risks of accident, safety, health, life and property of the employer’s family and his/her own.
4. To denounce to competent agencies if the employer commits acts of mistreating, sexually harassing or forcing labor or any other illegal acts.
Article 165. Prohibited acts of employers
1. Mistreating, sexually harassing, forcing labor and using violence against the domestic employee.
2. Assigning work to the domestic employees not in accordance with the labor contract.
3. Keeping personal documents of the domestic employee.
SECTION 6
OTHER TYPES OF EMPLOYEES
Article 166. Persons working in the fields of art, physical training, sports, maritime and aviation

Persons who work in the fields of arts, physical training, sports, maritime and aviation are entitled to some suitable regimes related to training, retraining for occupational qualification and skill improvement; labor contracts; wage and bonus; working time and rest time; and occupational safety and hygiene as stipulated by the Government.
Article 167. Employees performing home-based work
Employees may negotiate with employers to perform home-based work.
CHAPTER XII
SOCIAL INSURANCE, HEALTH INSURANCE AND UNEMPLOYEMENT INSURANCE
Article 168. Participation in social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance

1. Employers and employees shall participate in compulsory social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance and are entitled to the benefits in accordance with the social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance laws.
Employers and employees are encouraged to participate in other different forms of social insurance for employees.
2. When an employee is absent from work and is covered by social insurance, the employer is not required to pay a wage to the employee, unless otherwise agreed by both parties.

3. For an employee who is not covered by compulsory social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance, the employer shall concurrently pay to the employee a wage and an amount which is equivalent to the level of contribution to compulsory social insurance, compulsory health insurance and unemployment insurance in accordance with the social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance laws.
Article 169. Age of retirement
1. An employee, who meets the conditions on the period of payment of social insurance as prescribed by the law on social insurance, is entitled to a pension when reaching the age of retirement.

2. The age of retirement for employees in normal working conditions shall be amended in accordance with the roadmap until male employees reach full 62 years old in 2028 and female employees reach full 60 years old in 2035.

Starting from 2021, the age of retirement for employees working in normal working conditions shall be at 60 years and 03 months of age for male employees and 55 years and 04 months of age for female employees; the age of retirement shall increase by 03 months per year for male employees and by 04 months per year for female employees.

3. An employee whose working capacity has been declined; who performs a specially heavy, hazardous or dangerous job or a heavy, hazardous or dangerous job; who works in a region facing exceptionally difficult socio-economic conditions shall be entitled to retire at a younger age, but shall not be more than 05 years earlier than the age defined in Clause 2 of this Article at the time of retirement, unless otherwise prescribed by the law.

4. An employee who has high professional and technical qualifications and other special cases may retire at an older age, but shall not be more than 05 years higher than the age specified in Clause 2 of this Article at the time of retirement, unless otherwise prescribed by the law.
5. The Government shall detail the regulations of this Article.
CHAPTER XIII
WORKERS’ REPRESENTATIVE ORGANIZATIONS
AT GRASSROOT LEVEL
Article 170. The right to establish, join and operate workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level
1. Employees shall have the right to establish, join and operate trade unions in accordance with the Law on Trade Union.
2. Employees of enterprises have the right to establish, join and operate the organization of employees at the enterprise as defined in Article 172, Article 173 and Article 174 of this Code.

3. Workers’ representative organizations as prescribed in Clause 1 and Clause 2 of this Article shall have equal rights and obligations in representing and protecting lawful rights and legitimate interests of employees in industrial relations.
Article 171. Grassroot-level trade unions under the system of Vietnam trade unions
1. Grassroots-level trade unions under the system of Vietnam trade unions shall be established in agencies, organizations, units and enterprises.
2. The establishment, dissolution, organization and operation of grassroots-level trade unions shall be conducted in accordance with the Law on Trade Unions.
Article 172. The establishment and participation of workers’ representative organization at an enterprise
1. A workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall be established and operated after a competent state agency grants it the registration.

The workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall be organized and operated in accordance with the National Constitution, laws and regulations; on the basis of voluntariness, self-management and transparency.

2. The registration of the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall be revoked if the organization violates principles and purposes of the organization as prescribed at Point b, Clause 1, Article 174 of this Code or if the workers’ representative organization at the enterprise cease to exist in cases of division, separation, consolidation, merging, or dissolution or the enterprise undergoes dissolution or bankruptcy.
3. In case that the workers’ representative organization at the enterprise join the Vietnam Trade union, the organization shall conform to regulations of the Law on Trade Unions.

4. The Government shall prescribe the dossier; competence and procedure for registration, procedure for granting registration, or revoking registration; shall perform state management on the finance and assets of workers’ representative organizations at enterprises; and shall prescribe the unification, mergence, separation, segregation and dissolution of such organizations.
Article 173. Board of leaders, and members of workers’ representative organization at an enterprise

1. At the time of registration, the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall gain the minimum threshold of membership working at the enterprise as prescribed by the Government’s regulations.

2. The board of leaders shall be elected by members of the workers’ representative organization at the enterprise. Members of the elected board of the workers’ representative organizations at the enterprise shall be Vietnamese employees who are working at the enterprise, are not in the period of penal liability examination or executing the punishment, and are not in the period when their recorded unspent offences have not been released due to committing any crimes against national security; crimes against freedom of human beings, crimes of infringement upon citizens’ democratic freedom; crimes against ownership rights in accordance with regulations prescribed in the Penal Code.
Article 174. Constitution of the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise
1. Constitution of the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall include the following main contents:
a) Name and address of the organization; symbol (if any)

b) Mandate, purposes and scope of organization shall be to protect lawful rights and legitimate interests of members of the organization in industrial relations at the enterprise; to resolve issues, together with employers, related to rights, obligations and interests of employees and employers; to establish a progressive, harmonious and stable industrial relations;
c) Requirements and procedures to join and withdraw from the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise.

A workers’ representative organization at an enterprise shall not concurrently comprise both rank-and-file employees and employees directly involved in decision-making process of working conditions, recruitment, labor discipline, termination of employment contracts or assignment of employees to perform other jobs.
d) Organizational structure, working tenure and representatives of organization;
dd) Principles of organization and operation;
e) Procedures for the adoption of decisions of the organization;

The following contents shall be decided by the majority of members: the adoption, amendment and supplement of the organization’s constitution; election and dismissal of the Head and members of the Board of leaders of the organization; the unification, mergence, separation, segregation and dissolution of organization; the participation in Vietnam General Confederation for Labor;
g) Membership fees, source of property and finance, and its usage and management of the organization.
The financial collection and expenditure of the workers’ representative organization at an enterprise must be monitored, documented and annually published to members of the organization.
h) Complaints and internal resolutions for complaints;
2. The Government shall detail regulations of this Article.
Article 175. Prohibited acts of employers related to the establishment, participation and operation of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level

1. Acts of discrimination against employees and members of workers’ representative organizations for the reason of establishment, joining and operation of workers’ representative organizations, including:
a) Requesting employees to join or not to join or to leave the workers’ representative organization as a requirement for their recruitment, engagement or extension of labor contracts;
b) Dismissing, disciplining, unilaterally terminating employment contracts, or rejecting to extend labor contracts or transferring employees to perform other jobs;
c) Discriminating over wages, working hours and other rights and obligations in the extent of industrial relations;
d) Creating obstacles and difficulties in works in order to obstruct the operation of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level.

2. Acts of interference and manipulation in the process of establishment, election, development of work plan and implementation of activities of workers’ representative organizations, including using financial support or using economic measures to undermine or weaken the functioning and performance of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level or to discriminate in favor of or against workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level.
Article 176. Rights of members of the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level
1. Members of the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level are entitled to the following rights:

a) To meet employees at workplace when they perform tasks of workers’ representative organizations. It must be ensured that the performing such tasks shall not have any effect on the normal operation of employers;
b) To meet employers to perform tasks representing workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level;
c) To allocate their working time, as prescribed in Clause 2 and Clause 3 of this Article, to perform tasks of workers’ representative organizations while remaining to be paid by the employers;
d) To be provided with guarantees in industrial relations and in the implementation of their representative functions in accordance with the law.

2. The Government shall prescribe the minimum time that an employer must share allocate all members of the Board of leaders of the workers’ representative organization at grass-root level to perform tasks of the organization on the basis of the number of members of this organization.

3. The workers’ representative organization at grassroot level and the employer shall negotiate about the additional time compared to the minimum time specified in Clause 2 of this Article and the way to use the working time for members of the Board of leaders of the workers’ representative organization at grassroot level in line with their actual conditions.
Article 177. Obligations of employers towards workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level

1. To create no obstructions and difficulties when employees conduct lawful activities to establish, join a workers’ representative organization and participate in the operation of this workers’ representative organization at grassroot level.
2. To recognize and respect rights of legally established workers’ representative organizations.

3. To reach written agreements with the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations in case where the employers unilaterally terminate employment contracts or transfer employees to perform other jobs or apply disciplinary measure of dismissal to employees who are elected members of the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations. If failing to reach such agreement, the two parties shall report to competent agencies on labor issues under provincial People’s Committee. After 30 days from the date of reporting to competent agencies on labor issues under provincial People’s Committee, employers shall be eligible for making decisions. If disagreeing with the decision of the employers, employees and the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations have the right to request labor dispute settlement in line with the procedure and order prescribed by the law.

4. To extend the labor contracts until the end of their working tenure for employees whose labor contracts expire while they are in the incumbent Board of leaders of a workers’ representative organization.
5. To perform other obligations in accordance with the law.
Article 178. Rights and obligations of workers’ representative organizations at grassroot level in industrial relations
1. To conduct collective bargaining with employers in accordance with regulations of this Code;
2. To participate in dialogues at workplace in accordance with regulations of this Code;

3. To consult over the formation and supervision of the implementation of wage scales, wage tables, determination of labor norms, wage payment regulations, bonus regulations, internal working regulations and other relevant issues related to the rights and obligations of employees who are members of the organizations.
4. To represent employees in labor disputes and in complaint resolution upon authorization of employees;
5. To organize and lead strikes under regulations of this Code;

6. To receive technical support of legally-operated agencies and organizations in Viet Nam for the comprehension of the Labor law, of formalities and procedures of the establishment of workers’ representative organizations and of performance of their representative activities in industrial relations after being granted registration.
7. To be provided by employers with a workspace, information, and to be given guarantees for necessary conditions for the operation of workers’ representative organizations.
8. To be entitled to other rights and obligations in line with the law.
CHAPTER XIV
SETTLEMENT OF LABOR DISPUTES
Section 1
GENERAL PROVISIONS ON THE SETTLEMENT
OF LABOR DISPUTES
Article 179. Labor disputes

1. Labor dispute is a dispute on rights, obligations and interests that arise among the parties in the process of establishing, implementing or terminating labor relations; or a dispute among worker’s representative organizations; or a dispute arising from relations that are directly related to industrial relations. Labor disputes shall include the following categories:

a) Individual labor disputes between an employer and an employee; between an employee and an enterprise or agency that sends the employee to work overseas on work contract; between a dispatched employee and a hiring party;
b) Right-based and interest-based collective labor disputes between one or several workers’ representative organizations and an employer or one or more employers’ organization(s);

2. A right-based collective labor dispute is a dispute between one or several workers’ representative organization(s) and an employer or one or more employers’ organization(s) that arises in the following cases:
a) Difference in the interpretation and the implementation of terms in collective bargaining agreements, internal working regulations, and other regulations and other lawful agreements;
b) Difference in the interpretation and the implementation of the labor law;

c) When an employer engages in an act of discrimination against employees, rank-and-file members and members of the Board of leaders of workers’ representative organizations for the reason of establishing and joining workers’ representative organizations and participating in workers’ representative organizations activities; or when an employer engages in an act of intervention or manipulation against workers’ representative organizations; or in an act of violation of the obligation to negotiate in good faith.
3. Right-based collective labor disputes shall include:
a) Labor disputes that arise during the process of collective bargaining;
b) When one party refuses to negotiate or does not conduct negotiations within the time limit as prescribed by the law.
Article 180. Principles of settlement of labor disputes
1. To respect the self-determination right through negotiation of the parties throughout the labor dispute settlement process.

2. To attach great importance to the settlement of labor disputes through mediation and arbitration on the basis of respect for the rights and interests of both disputing parties, of respect for the common interest of the society and the compliance with the law;
3. To guarantee publicity, transparency, objectiveness, timeliness, quickness and lawfulness.
4. To ensure the participation of representative sof each party in the labor dispute settlement process.

5. The settlement of a labor dispute shall be conducted by a competent agency, organization or person upon request from the disputing parties or upon request from competent agencies, organizations and individuals and agreed by the disputing parties.
Article 181. Responsibilities of agencies and organizations in the settlement of labor disputes

1. The state management agency of labor shall coordinate with the workers’ representative organization and the employers’ representative organization in providing guidance and assistance to the disputing parties during the labor dispute settlement.
2. The Ministry of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall organize training to raise professional capacity for labor conciliators and arbitrators in settling labor disputes.

3. Upon request for labor dispute settlement, competent agencies on labor under People’s Committee shall be the focal point to receive the request for labor disputes settlement, shall take the responsibility for classifying, providing guidance and support to the disputing parties in the labor dispute settlement.

Within 05 working days, agencies in charge of receiving requests for labor disputes settlement shall send these requests to labor conciliators in case that these labor disputes must go through the labor conciliation; or shall send these requests to the Labor Arbitration Council upon request or shall provide guidance to send these requests to the People’s Court for settlement.
Article 182. Rights and obligations of the two disputing parties in labor dispute settlement
1. During the labor dispute settlement, the two parties have the following rights:
a) To participate directly or through a representative in the settlement process;
b) To withdraw or change the content of their written request;
c) To request change of the person in charge of settling the labor dispute if they have grounds to believe that such person may not be impartial or objective.
2. During the labor dispute settlement, the two disputing parties shall have the following obligations:
a) To promptly and fully provide all documents and evidence to prove their request;
