b) To abide by the reached agreement, the judgment of the Board of Labor Conciliators or the ruling of People’s Court which has taken legal effect.
Article 183. Powers of competent agencies, organizations and individuals in the settlement of labor disputes

Agencies, organizations and persons competent to settle labor disputes may, within the scope of their tasks and powers, shall request the two disputing parties and relevant agencies, organizations and individuals to provide documents and evidence, solicit assessment and invite witnesses and other related people.
Article 184. Labor conciliators

1. Labor conciliators are appointed by the Chairperson of a provincial People’s Committee to conciliate labor disputes, and disputes over vocational training contracts; and to support the development of industrial relations.

2. The Government shall prescribe the criteria, procedures and formalities for the appointment of conciliators; working conditions and management of labor conciliators; and competence, procedures and formalities for sending labor conciliators.
Article 185. Labor Arbitration Council

1. The chairperson of a provincial-level People’s Committee shall decide to establish the Labor Arbitration Council and to appoint its Chairperson, a secretary and labor arbitrators of the Labor Arbitration Council. The working term of the Labor Arbitration Council shall be 5 years.

2. The number of arbitrators of the Labor Arbitration Council shall be decided by the Chairperson of the provincial People’s Committee, consisting of at least 15 members, including equal proportions nominated by each party, specifically:

a) At least 05 members nominated by the competent agency on labor under the provincial People’s Committee, of which the Chairperson of the Council is the representative leader from this agency and the Council secretary is an official of this agency.
b) At least 05 members nominated by the provincial federation of labor;
c) At least 05 members nominated by employers’ representative organizations in the province.
3. Criteria and working regime of labor arbitrators shall be prescribed as follows:
a) Labor arbitrators must have knowledge of laws, experiences in industrial relations, and must be creditable and impartial;

b) When nominating labor arbitrators under regulations in Clause 2 of this Article, the competent agency on labor under the provincial People’s Committee, the provincial federation of labor, and employers’ representative organizations may nominate their officials and other people meeting the criteria of labor arbitrators under legal regulations;
c) The Secretary of the Labor Arbitration Council shall work full-time at the Labor Arbitration Council. Labor arbitrators may work on full-time or part-time basis.

4. Upon a request to settle labor disputes under regulations in Article 189, Article 193 and Article 197 of this Code, the Labor Arbitration Council shall establish an Arbitration Panel to settle labor disputes as follows:
a) Representative of each disputing party shall select one arbitrator in the list of labor arbitrators.
b) Labor arbitrators selected by disputing parties as prescribed at Point a of this Clause shall nominate 01 other labor arbitrator to be the Head of the Arbitration Panel;
c) In case all disputing parties select the same arbitrator to settle labor disputes, the Arbitration Panel shall include only 01 arbitrator;
5. The Arbitration Panel shall operate on the principle of collectivism and the rule of majority, except for cases specified at Point c, Clause 4 of this Article;

6. The Government shall prescribe in details for the criteria, procedures, and formalities for the appointment and dismissal of arbitrators, working conditions for labor arbitrators and the Labor Arbitration Council; the establishment and operation of the Labor Arbitration Council; and the organization and operation of the Arbitration Panel as defined at this Article.
Article 186. Prohibition of unilateral acts pending settlement of labor disputes

None of the disputing parties are allowed to take unilateral actions against the other party pending the settlement of their labor disputes by a competent agency, organization or individual in the time limit as prescribed by this Code.
SECTION 2
COMPETENCE AND PROCEDURES FOR THE SETTLEMENT OF INDIVIDUAL LABOR DISPUTES
Article 187. Competence for the settlement of individual labor disputes
Agencies, organizations and individuals who are competent to resolve individual labor disputes shall include:
1. The Labor conciliator;
2. The Labor Arbitration Council;
3. The People’s Court.
Article 188. Procedures for the settlement of individual labor disputes by labor conciliators

1. Individual labor disputes must go through the conciliation conducted by labor conciliators before going to the Labour Arbitration Council or the People’s court for settlement, except the following labor disputes:
a) Disputes over disciplinary measures of dismissal or unilateral termination of labor contracts;
b) Disputes over compensation for damage and allowance upon termination of labor contracts;
c) Disputes between a domestic employee and his/her employer;

d) Disputes over social insurance in accordance with the law on social insurance, disputes over health insurance in accordance with the law on health insurance, disputes over unemployment insurance in accordance with the law on employment, disputes over insurance against work accident or occupational disease in accordance with the law on occupational safety and hygiene;
dd) Disputes over compensation between employees and enterprises or agencies sending employees to work abroad under contracts.
e) Disputes between dispatched employees and their employers;

2. Within 05 working days from the date of receiving a conciliation request from disputing parties or from competent agencies as defined in Clause 3, Article 181 of this Code, the labor conciliator shall complete the conciliation.
3. Both disputing parties must be present at the conciliation meeting. The disputing parties may authorize their representatives to attend the conciliation meeting.
4. The labor conciliator shall instruct and support the disputing parties to negotiate and settle disputes.

In case the two parties can reach an agreement, the labor conciliator shall prepare a record of successful conciliation. The record of successful conciliation must be signed by disputing parties and the labor conciliator.

In case the two parties cannot reach any agreement, the labor conciliator shall recommend a solution to the parties for consideration. In case the two parties agree with the recommended solution, the labor conciliator shall prepare a record of successful conciliation. The record of successful conciliation must be signed by disputing parties and the labor conciliator.

In case the parties do not agree with the recommended solution or one of the disputing parties is absent without a plausible reason after having been duly summoned for two times, the labor conciliator shall prepare a record of unsuccessful conciliation. The record of unsuccessful conciliation must be signed by disputing parties and the labor conciliator.
5. Copies of the record of successful or unsuccessful conciliation must be sent to all disputing parties within 01 working day from the date the record is made.

6. In case either party does not implement the agreement written in the record of successful conciliation, the other disputing party has the right to request settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council or a court.

7. In case where conciliation is not required as specified at Clause 1 of this Article or where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article or in case of unsuccessful conciliation as specified in Clause 4 of this Article, the disputing parties shall have the right to choose one of the following methods to settle labor disputes:
a) To request the Arbitration Council for settlement as prescribed in Article 189 of this Code;
b) To request the Court for settlement.
Article 189. Settlement of individual labor disputes by the Labor Arbitration Council

1. On the basis of mutual agreement, the disputing parties may request dispute settlement by a Labor Arbitration Council in cases as prescribed in Clause 7, Article 188 of this Code. When the parties have requested the Labor Arbitration Council to resolve the dispute, they are not allowed to request for dispute settlement by the Court during the duration that the Labor Arbitration Council is resolving the dispute, except for the cases specified in Clause 4 of this Article.
2. Within 07 working days after receiving the request for dispute settlement as specified in Clause 1 of this Article, an Arbitration panel shall be established for dispute settlement.
3. Within 30 working days after the Arbitration Panel is established, this panel must issue a judgement on the dispute settlement and send this judgement to the disputing parties.

4. In case where the Arbitration Panel is not established within the time limit as prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article or the Arbitration Panel fails to resolve the dispute within the time limit as prescribed at Clause 3 of this Article, the parties shall have the right to request for the dispute settlement by the People’s Court.

5. In case where one of the disputing parties does not comply with the judgement on the dispute settlement of the Arbitration Panel, other parties have the right to request for the dispute settlement by the Court.
Article 190. Time limit for requesting the settlement of individual labor disputes

1. The time limit to request a labor conciliator to settle an individual labor dispute is 06 months from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected.

2. The time limit to request the settlement of an individual dispute by the Labor Arbitration Council is 09 months from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected.

3. The time limit to bring an individual labor dispute to the People’s Court is 01 year from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected.

4. In case the requesting party can prove that due to a force majeure event, an objective obstacle or other reason prescribed by law it cannot request the settlement of an individual labor dispute within the time limit as prescribed in this Article, the time of the force majeure event or the objective obstacle or the reason shall not be included in the statute of limitations for requesting the settlement of the individual labor dispute.
SECTION 3
COMPETENCE AND PROCEDURES FOR THE SETTLEMENT OF RIGHT-BASED COLLECTIVE LABOR DISPUTES
Article 191. Competence for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes
1. Agencies, organizations and individuals who are competent to settle right-based collective labor disputes shall include:
a) The Labor conciliator;
b) The Labor Arbitration Council;
c) The People’s Court.

2. Right-based collective labor disputes must be settled through conciliation procedures of labor conciliators before requesting for the settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council or the People’s Court.
Article 192. Procedures and formalities for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes
1. Procedures and formalities for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes shall be implemented under regulations in Clauses 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of Article 188 of this Code;

For disputes defined at Point b and Point c, Clause 2, Article 179 of this Code with violations of law detected, the labor conciliator shall prepare a record and send the dossier and documents to competent agencies for consideration and handling in accordance with the law.

2. In case of unsuccessful conciliation or in case where the labor conciliator fails to conduct conciliation within the time limit as specified in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code, the disputing parties shall have the right to choose one of the following methods to settle labor disputes:
a) To request the Labor Arbitration Council for settlement as prescribed in Article 193 of this Code;
b) To request the Court for settlement.
Article 193. Settlement of right-based collective labor disputes by the Labor Arbitration Council

1. In case of unsuccessful conciliation; in case where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code; or in case where either party does not implement the agreement written in the record of successful conciliation - the disputing parties, on the basis of mutual agreement, may request the dispute settlement by a Labor Arbitration Council.
2. Within 07 working days after receiving the request for dispute settlement as specified in Clause 1 of this Article, an Arbitration Panel shall be established for settling disputes.

3. Within 30 working days after the Arbitration Panel is established, on the basis of provisions of labor law, collective bargaining agreements and registered internal work rules and other lawful agreements and regulations, this Panel must issue a judgement on the dispute settlement and send this judgement to the disputing parties.

For disputes defined at Point b and Point c, Clause 2, Article 179 of this Code with violations of law, the labor conciliator shall not issue any judgement but shall prepare a record and send the dossier and documents to competent agencies for consideration and handling in accordance with the law.

4. In case the disputing parties choose to have the Labor Arbitration Council settle their disputes under regulations of this Article, during the process of dispute settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council, the disputing parties must not request for the settlement of the People’s Court.

5. In case where an Arbitration Panel is not established within the time limit as prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article or the Arbitration Panel fails to resolve the dispute within the time limit as prescribed at Clause 3 of this Article, the parties shall have the right to request for the dispute settlement by the Court.

6. In case where one of the disputing parties does not comply with the judgement on the dispute settlement of the Arbitration Panel, other parties have the right to request for the dispute settlement by the People’s Court.
Article 194. Time limit for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes

1. The time limit to request a labor conciliator to settle a right-based collective labor dispute is 06 months from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected.

2. The time limit to request the settlement of a right-based collective labor dispute by the Labor Arbitration Council is 09 months from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected.

3. The time limit to bring a right-based collective labor dispute to the People’s Court is 01 year from the date on which the act, which a party claims has caused the infringement of the lawful rights or interests, is detected.
SECTION 4
COMPETENCE AND PROCEDURES FOR THE SETTLEMENT OF RIGHT-BASED LABOR DISPUTES
Article 195. Competence for the settlement of interest-based collective labor disputes
1. Agencies, organizations and individuals who are competent to settle interest-based collective labor disputes shall include:
a) The Labor conciliator;
b) The Labor Arbitration Council;

2. Interest-based collective labor disputes must be settled through conciliation procedures of labor conciliators before requesting for the settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council or carrying out procedures for going on strike.
Article 196. Procedures and formalities for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes
1. Procedures and formalities for the settlement of right-based collective labor disputes shall comply with regulations in Clauses 2, 3, 4 and 5, Article 188 of this Code;

2. In case of successful conciliation, the record of successful conciliation shall include all contents agreed upon by all disputing parties, and signatures of those parties and the labor conciliator. The record of successful conciliation shall be considered as a legal document of the enterprise’s collective bargaining agreement.

3. In case of unsuccessful conciliation, in case where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code; or in case where either party does not implement the agreement written in the record of successful conciliation, the disputing parties have the right to choose one of the following methods to settle their labor disputes:
a) To request the Arbitration Council for settlement as prescribed in Article 197 of this Code;
b) Worker’s representative organizations have the right to conduct procedures for going on a strike as prescribed in Articles 200, 201, and 202 of this Code.
Article 197. Settlement of interest-based collective labor disputes by the Labor Arbitration Council

1. In case of unsuccessful conciliation; in case where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code; or in case where either party does not implement the agreement written in the record of successful conciliation - the disputing parties, on the basis of mutual agreement, may request the dispute settlement by a Labor Arbitration Council.
2. Within 07 working days after receiving the request for dispute settlement as specified in Clause 1 of this Article, an Arbitration Panel shall be established for dispute settlement.

3. Within 30 working days after the Arbitration panel is established, on the basis of provisions of labor law, collective bargaining agreements and registered internal work rules and other lawful agreements and regulations, this panel must issue a judgement on the dispute settlement and send this judgement to the disputing parties.

4. In case the disputing parties choose to have the Labor Arbitration Council settle their disputes under regulations of this Article, during the process of dispute settlement by the Labor Arbitration Council, the disputing parties must not carry out a strike.

In case where a Labor Arbitration Panel is not established within the time limit as prescribed in Clause 2 of this Article or the Labor Arbitration Panel fails to resolve the dispute within the time limit as prescribed at Clause 3 of this Article, or employers as a disputing party does not conform to the judgement of the Labor Arbitration Panel, the workers’ representative organization as a disputing party shall have the right to conduct procedures as prescribed in Articles 200, 201 and 202 of this Code for going on a strike.
SECTION 5
STRIKE
Article 198. Strike

1. Strike is a temporary, voluntary and organized work stoppage of an employees’ collective in order to achieve their demands in the process of labor dispute settlement. Strikes are organized and led by the workers’ representative organization, who has the right to conduct collective bargaining, as a disputing party.
Article 199. Cases where employees shall have the right to strike

A workers’ representative organization as a disputing party in an interest-based labor dispute shall conduct the procedures as prescribed in Articles 200, 201 and 202 of this Code to go on a strike in the following cases:
1. In case of unsuccessful conciliation or in case where the labor conciliator fails to resolve the disputes within the time limits as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 188 of this Code;

2. In case where a Labor Arbitration Panel is not established within the time limit; in case where the Labor Arbitration Panel is established but this Panel fails to resolve the dispute; or in case the employer as a disputing party does not conform to the judgement of the Labor Arbitration Panel.
Article 200. Sequence of going on strike
1. Collecting opinions on the strike as prescribed in Article 201 of this Code;
2. Issuing a decision to go on strike and a notice of strike as prescribed in Article 202 of this Code;
3. Going on strike.
Article 201. Collecting opinions on the strike

1. Before commencing a strike, the workers’ representative organization which has the right to organize and lead a strike as prescribed in Article 198 of this Code shall take the responsibility for collecting opinions of all employees or members of the Board of leaders of the workers’ representative organization participating in the negotiation.
2. Issues to be put up for opinions on going on a strike include:
a) Approval or disapproval of the strike;
b) The option suggested by the workers’ representative organization on the contents specified at Points b, c and d, Clause 2, Article 202 of this Code;
3. Opinions may be collected by ballot or signatures or other prescribed methods.

4. The time, venue and method of collecting opinions on going on a strike must be determined by the workers’ representative organization and must be notified to the employer at least 01 day in advance. The solicitation of opinion must not leave adverse impacts on the normal business and manufacturing operation of the employer. The employer must not create any obstructions, difficulties or intervention in the solicitation of opinions on the strike conducted by the workers’ representative organization.
Article 202. Decision of going on a strike and notification of the starting time of a strike

1. When over 50% of the consulted employees agree with the matters of strike putting forward for opinions as prescribed in Clause 2, Article 201 of this Code, the workers’ representative organization shall issue a written decision to go on strike.
2. A decision to go on strike must include:
a) The outcome of the collection of opinions on going on strike;
b) The starting time and venue for the strike;
c) Scope of the strike;
d) Demands of the employees;
e) Full name and address of the representative of the workers’ representative organization organizing and leading the strike.

3. At least 05 working days prior to the starting date of the strike, the workers’ representative organization organizing and leading the strike shall send the decision to go on strike to the employer, district-level People’s Committee and the competent agency on labor under provincial People’s Committee.
4. By the starting time of the strike, if the employer does not accept the demands of the employees, the workers’ representative organization may organize and lead the strike.
Article 203. Rights of the parties prior to and during a strike
1. To continue negotiating to settle the collective labor dispute or jointly request a labor conciliator or the Labor Arbitration Council to settle labor disputes.
2. The workers’ representative organization organizing and leading a strike as prescribed in Article 198 of this Code shall have the following rights:
a) To withdraw the decision to go on strike if the strike has not happened yet or to stop the strike if it is happening;
b) To request the Court to declare the strike is legal.
3. The employer shall have the following rights:
a) To accept the demand entirely or in parts, and send a written notice of his/her acceptance to the workers’ representative organization that organizes and leads the strike;
b) To temporarily close the workplace during the strike due to shortage of conditions to maintain normal operations or to protect the assets;
c) To request the Court to declare the strike is illegal.
Article 204. Cases in which a strike is illegal
1. The strike does not fall into any cases prescribed in Article 199 of this Code.
2. The strike is not organized and led by a workers’ representative organization which have the right to organize and lead a strike.
3. The strike violates regulations on procedures and formalities to go on strikes in accordance with this Code;
4. When the labor dispute is being settled by competent agencies, organizations and individuals under provisions of this Code;
5. The strike is conducted in case where a strike is prohibited as prescribed in Article 209 of this Code;
6. The strike occurs when the decision to postpone or cancel the strike has been issued by competent agencies in accordance with provisions in Article 210 of this Code;
Article 205. Notice of the decision on temporary closure of the workplace

At least 03 working days before the date of temporary closure of the workplace, the decision on temporary closure must be publicly posted up at the workplace and notified by the employer to the following agencies and organizations:
1. The workers’ representative organization that is organizing and leading the strike;
2. The provincial-level People’s Committee of the locality where the workplace is located;
3. The district-level People’s Committee of the locality where the work place is located.
Article 206. Prohibited cases of temporary closure of the workplace
1. 12 hours prior to the starting time of the strike notified in the decision to go on strike.
2. After the employees stop striking.
Article 207. Wages and other lawful interests of employees during a strike

1. Employees who do not take part in a strike but have to stop working because of the strike shall be paid with a work suspension allowance under Clause 2, Article 99 of this Code and other benefits prescribed in the labor law.
2. Employees taking part in a strike may not be paid with wages or other benefits as prescribed by the law, unless otherwise agreed by both parties.
Article 208. Prohibited acts before, during and after a strike
1. Obstructing employees to exercise their rights to go on strike or instigating, dragging or forcing employees to go on strike, and preventing non-strikers from going to work.
2. Using violence; sabotaging machines, equipment and assets of the employer.
3. Violating public order and security.

4. Terminating the labor contracts with, or imposing labor disciplinary measures on employees and strike leaders or transferring employees and strike leaders to other jobs or other locations due to their preparation for or their involvement in the strike.
5. Taking revenge actions on employees who are on strike or leaders of the strike.
6. Taking advantage of the strike to commit other illegal acts.
Article 209. Workplaces where strikes are prohibited
1. Strike is prohibited in working places where strikes can threaten the national defense, public security, social order and human health.

2. The Government shall detail the list of workplaces where strikes are prohibited and the settlement of labor disputes in workplaces where strikes are prohibited as specified in Clause 1 of this Article.
Article 210. Decisions to postpone or cancel strikes

1. When considering that a strike may cause serious damage to the national economy and public interests or may threaten national defense, public security, social order and human health, the Chairperson of the provincial-level People’s Committee shall decide to postpone or cancel such strike.
2. The Government shall detail regulations on the postponement and cancellation of strikes and the settlement of interests of the employees.
Article 211. Handling of strikes that do not follow the prescribed sequence and procedures

Within 12 hours after receiving the notification of a strike that does not comply with regulations in Articles 200, 201 and 202 of this Code, the Chairperson of the district-level People’s Committee shall assume the prime responsibility for, guide the competent agency on labor, and collaborate with the trade union at the same level and other relevant agencies and organizations in, holding a meeting directly with the employer and the representatives of the grassroots-level workers’ representative organization to consult and support the parties to find solutions to the case and resume normal production and business operations.

In case of detecting acts of law violation, make a record, handle or propose competent agencies to handle individuals and organizations that have committed acts of law violation according to law provisions.
With regard to the content of a labor dispute, depending on the type of dispute, to guide and assist the parties to conduct labor dispute settlement procedures in accordance with this Code.
CHAPTER XV
STATE MANAGEMENT OF LABOR
Article 212. Contents of state management of labor
1. Promulgating and implementing legal documents on labor.

2. Monitoring, making statistics and providing information on labor supply and demand and fluctuations of labor supply and demand; making decision on policies, master plans and plans on human resources, distribution and utilization of labor in the whole society, vocational training, development of vocational skills; formulating the national vocational qualification framework and the national qualification framework for levels of vocational training. Issuing a list of jobs that require employees who have been vocationally trained or possess national vocational skills certificates;

3. Organizing and conducting scientific research on labor; collecting statistics and information on labor and the labor market and on the living standards, wages and income level of employees; managing the labor quality, quantity and labor fluctuation.

4. Building mechanisms and institutions to support the development of harmonious, stable and progressive industrial relations; promote the implementation of the regulations of this Code towards employees without industrial relations; conducting the registration and management of the operation of workers’ representative organizations at enterprises.
5. Inspecting, examining, settling complaints and denunciations and handling violations of the labor law; and settling labor disputes in accordance with the law.
6. International cooperation in the field of labor.
Article 213. Competence of state management of labor
1. The Government shall uniformly perform the state management of labor nationwide.
2. The Ministry of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs shall take responsibility before the Government for performing the state management of labor.

3. Ministries and ministerial-level agencies shall, within the ambit of their tasks and powers, perform and coordinate with the Ministry of Labor, War Invalids and Social Affairs in performing the state management of labor.
4. People’s Committees at all levels shall perform the state management of labor within their respective localities.
CHAPTER XVI
LABOR INSPECTION, HANDLING OF VIOLATIONS OF
LABOR LAW
Article 214. Contents of labor inspection
1. To inspect the compliance with the labor law;
2. To investigate labor accidents and violations of occupational safety and hygiene;
3. To guide the application of the system of standards and technical regulations on working conditions and occupational safety and hygiene;
4. To settle labor-related complaints and denunciations in accordance with law;
5. To handle violations of labor law within the ambit of their competence.
Article 215. Labor inspection
1. The specialized inspection of labor shall be conducted in accordance with the Law on Inspection.
2. The inspection of occupational safety and hygiene shall be conducted in accordance with the Law on Occupational Safety and Hygiene.
Article 216. Rights of labor inspectors
Labor inspectors shall have the right to inspect and investigate workplaces within the scope of the assigned subject and the scope of inspection in accordance with the inspection decision.

Any unexpected inspection in accordance with the decision issued by a competent person - in case of emergency which might threaten the safety, life, health, honor and dignity of the employees at workplace – might be conducted without prior notice.
Article 217. Handling of violations

1. Any person violating the provisions of this Code shall, depending on the seriousness of their violations, be disciplined, administratively sanctioned or examined for penal liability; and, if causing any damage, shall pay compensations in accordance with law.

2. When the Court issues the ruling that the strike is illegal, the employees on strike shall immediately stop going on strike and return to work; in case the employees still continue to go on strike and do not return to work, depending on the seriousness of their violation, they may be subject to disciplinary measures in accordance with the labor law.
In case an illegal strike causes damage to the employer, the damage must be compensated in accordance with law by the workers’ representative organization that organizes and leads the strike.

3. Those who take advantage of a strike to cause public disorder, sabotage machines and assets of the employer; those who prevent or instigate, drag or force employees to go on strike; those who take revenge on strikers and leaders of the strike, shall, depending on the seriousness of their violations, be administratively sanctioned or examined for penal liability; and, if causing any damage, shall pay compensations in accordance with law.
CHAPTER XVII
IMPLEMENTATION PROVISIONS
Article 218. Exemption and reduction of procedures in cases of employing under 10 employees
Employer who employ under 10 employees shall comply with this Code but a number of procedures shall be exempted or reduced as prescribed by the Government.
Article 219. Amendment ad supplement to a number of articles related to labor

2. To amend and supplement Article 32 of the Civil Procedure Code No. 92/2015/QH13 as follows:
a) To amend and supplement the title of the Article and Clause 1; to add Clause 1a, 1b and 1c after Clause 1 as follows:
Article 32. Labor disputes and other labor-related disputes within the jurisdiction of the Court

1. Individual labor disputes between an employee and an employer, which have been successfully conciliated by labor conciliators but the parties fail to comply or fail to properly comply with the conciliation results, or which cannot be conciliated, or which are not conciliated within the time limit as prescribed by Law, except the following labor disputes which are not required to be conciliated:

b) Disputes over compensation for damages or over allowance upon termination of a labor contract;
c) Disputes between a domestic employee and his/her employer;

d) Disputes over social insurance in accordance with the social insurance law; over health insurance in accordance with the health insurance law; over unemployment insurance in accordance with the employment law; or over occupational accident or disease insurance in accordance with the occupational safety and health law;
dd) Disputes over compensation for damages between a worker and an enterprise or a non-business unit that sends the worker to work overseas under a contract;
e) Disputes between a dispatched employee and his/her employer;

1a. In case where individual labor disputes are agreed by the disputing parties to be settled by the Labor Arbitration Council but the Labor Arbitration Panel fails to be established within the time limit as prescribed by the labor law or the Labor Arbitration Panel is established but this Panel fails to resolve the dispute; or in case the employer as a disputing party does not conform to the judgement of the Labor Arbitration Panel – the disputing parties shall have the right to request the settlement of the Court.

1b. In case where right-based collective labor disputes which have been though the conciliation procedure of a labor conciliator but the labor conciliator fails to settle these disputes or the labor conciliator fails to conduct conciliation within the time limit as prescribed by the labor law, the disputing parties shall have the right to request the settlement of the Court.

1c. In case where interest-based collective labor disputes are agreed by the disputing parties to be settled by the Labor Arbitration Council but the Labor Arbitration Panel fails to be established within the time limit as prescribed by the labor law or the Labor Arbitration Panel is established but this Panel fails to resolve the dispute; or in case the employer as a disputing party does not conform to the judgement of the Labor Arbitration Panel – the disputing parties shall have the right to request the settlement of the Court.”;
b) To annul Clause 2 of Article 32.
Article 220. Effect
1. This Code takes effect from January 01, 2021.
The Labor Code No.10/2012/QH13 shall be annulled from the date on which this Code takes effect.

2. From the date on which this Code takes effect, labor contracts, collective labor bargaining and other legitimate agreements whose contents are not against the law or whose contents ensure employees to have more favorable rights and conditions than those prescribed in this Code shall continue to be implemented, except cases where concerned parties reach an agreement on the amendment and supplement to comply with and to implement regulation of this Code;

3. Labor policies for cadres, civil servants, public employees, members of the People’s Army and People’s Public Security forces and other social organizations, members of cooperatives and employees with no industrial relation shall be prescribed by other legal documents, but depending on each category, some provisions of this Code may be applied.
